* '''1969'''&nbsp;– [[Charles Misner]] formally presents the Big Bang [[horizon problem]].
* '''1969'''&nbsp;– Robert Dicke formally presents the Big Bang flatness problem.
* '''1970'''&nbsp;– [[Vera Rubin]] and Kent Ford measure spiral galaxy rotation curves at large radii, showing evidence for substantial amounts of [[dark matter]].
* '''1973'''&nbsp;– [[Edward Tryon]] proposes that the universe may be a large scale [[quantum mechanics|quantum mechanical]] [[quantum fluctuation|vacuum fluctuation]] where positive mass-energy is balanced by negative [[gravitational energy|gravitational potential energy]].
* '''1976'''&nbsp;– [[Alexander Shlyakhter]] uses [[samarium]] ratios from the [[Oklo]] prehistoric [[natural nuclear fission reactor]] in [[Gabon]] to show that some laws of physics have remained unchanged for over two billion years.
* '''1977'''&nbsp;– [[Gary Steigman]], [[David Schramm (astrophysicist)|David Schramm]], and [[James Gunn (astronomer)|James Gunn]] examine the relation between the primordial helium abundance and number of neutrinos and claim that at most five [[lepton]] families can exist.
* '''1980'''&nbsp;– [[Alan Guth]] and Alexei Starobinsky independently propose the [[cosmic inflation|inflationary]] Big Bang universe as a possible solution to the horizon and flatness problems.
* '''1981'''&nbsp;– [[Viatcheslav Mukhanov]] and G. Chibisov propose that quantum fluctuations could lead to large scale structure in an [[cosmic inflation|inflationary]] universe.
* '''1982'''&nbsp;– The first CfA galaxy redshift survey is completed.
* '''1982'''&nbsp;– Several groups including [[Jim Peebles|James Peebles]], J. Richard Bond and George Blumenthal propose that the universe is dominated by cold [[dark matter]].
* '''1983–1987''' &nbsp;– The first large computer simulations of cosmic structure formation are run by Davis, Efstathiou, Frenk and White. The results show that cold dark matter produces a reasonable match to observations, but hot dark matter does not.
[[File:Egret all sky gamma ray map from CGRO spacecraft.png|thumb|275px|The sky at energies above 100 MeV observed by the [[Energetic Gamma Ray Experiment Telescope]] (EGRET) of the [[Compton Gamma Ray Observatory]] (CGRO) satellite (1991&ndash;2000).]]
* '''1988'''&nbsp;– The [[CfA2 Great Wall]] is discovered in the CfA2 redshift survey.
* '''1988'''&nbsp;– Measurements of galaxy large-scale flows provide evidence for the [[Great Attractor]].
* '''1990'''&nbsp;– The [[Hubble Space Telescope]] is launched.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://science.ksc.nasa.gov/shuttle/missions/sts-31/mission-sts-31.html |title=STS-31 |publisher=NASA |access-date=April 26, 2008 |archive-date=August 15, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110815191242/http://science.ksc.nasa.gov/shuttle/missions/sts-31/mission-sts-31.html |url-status=live }}</ref> It is aimed primarily at deep-space objects.
* '''1990'''&nbsp;– Preliminary results from [[NASA]]'s [[Cosmic Background Explorer|COBE]] mission confirm the [[cosmic microwave background radiation]] has a [[blackbody]] spectrum to an astonishing one part in 10<sup>5</sup> precision, thus eliminating the possibility of an integrated starlight model proposed for the background by steady state enthusiasts.
* '''1992'''&nbsp;– Further [[Cosmic Background Explorer|COBE]] measurements discover the very small [[anisotropy]] of the [[cosmic microwave background]], providing a "baby picture" of the seeds of large-scale structure when the universe was around 1/1100th of its present size and 380,000 years old.
* '''1992'''&nbsp;– First [[planetary system]] beyond the Solar System detected, around the [[pulsar]] [[PSR B1257+12]].<ref>{{cite journal |bibcode=1992Natur.355..145W |author=Wolszczan, A. |author2=Frail, D. |title=A planetary system around the millisecond pulsar PSR1257 + 12 |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=355 |issue=6356 |pages=145–147 |date=1992 |doi=10.1038/355145a0 |s2cid=4260368}}</ref>
* '''1995'''&nbsp;– The first planet around a Sun-like star is discovered, in orbit around the star [[51 Pegasi]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mayor |first1=Michael |last2=Queloz |first2=Didier |title=A Jupiter-mass companion to a solar-type star |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |date=1995 |volume=378 |issue=6555 |pages=355–359 |doi=10.1038/378355a0 |bibcode = 1995Natur.378..355M |s2cid=4339201 }}</ref>
* '''1996'''&nbsp;– The first [[Hubble Deep Field]] is released, providing a clear view of very distant galaxies when the universe was around one-third of its present age.
* '''1998'''&nbsp;– Controversial evidence for the [[fine-structure constant]] varying over the lifetime of the universe is first published.
* '''1998'''&nbsp;– The [[Supernova Cosmology Project]] and [[High-Z Supernova Search Team]]  discover [[dark energy|cosmic acceleration]] based on distances to [[Type Ia supernova]]e, providing the first direct evidence for a non-zero [[cosmological constant]].
* '''1999'''&nbsp;– Measurements of the [[cosmic microwave background radiation]] with finer resolution than COBE, (most notably by the [[BOOMERanG experiment]] see Mauskopf et al., 1999, Melchiorri et al., 1999, de Bernardis et al. 2000) provide evidence for oscillations (the first acoustic peak) in the [[anisotropy]] angular spectrum, as expected in the standard model of cosmological structure formation. The angular position of this peak indicates that the geometry of the universe is close to flat.

==2001–present==
* '''2001'''&nbsp;– The [[2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey]] (2dF) by an Australian/British team gave strong evidence that the matter density is near 25% of critical density. Together with the CMB results for a flat universe, this provides independent evidence for a [[cosmological constant]] or similar [[dark energy]].
* '''2002'''&nbsp;– The [[Cosmic Background Imager]] (CBI) in [[Chile]] obtained images of the cosmic microwave background radiation with the highest angular resolution of 4 arc minutes. It also obtained the anisotropy spectrum at high-resolution not covered before up to l ~ 3000. It found a slight excess in power at high-resolution (l > 2500) not yet completely explained, the so-called "CBI-excess".
* '''2003'''&nbsp;– NASA's [[Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe]] (WMAP) obtained full-sky detailed pictures of the cosmic microwave background radiation. The images can be interpreted to indicate that the universe is 13.7 billion years old (within one percent error), and are very consistent with the [[Lambda-CDM model]] and the density fluctuations predicted by [[cosmic inflation|inflation]].
[[Image:Cosmic Background Imager- CMB.png|right|220px|thumb|[[Cosmic microwave background]] as measured by the [[Cosmic Background Imager]] experiment.]]
* '''2003'''&nbsp;– The [[Sloan Great Wall]] is discovered.
* '''2004'''&nbsp;– The Degree Angular Scale Interferometer (DASI) first obtained the E-mode polarization spectrum of the cosmic microwave background radiation.
* '''2004'''&nbsp;– ''[[Voyager 1]]'' sends back the first data ever obtained from within the Solar System's [[heliosheath]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://solarsystem.nasa.gov/news/display.cfm?News_ID=36121 |title=Voyager 1 Sees Solar Wind Decline |publisher=NASA |date=December 13, 2010 |access-date=September 16, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110614073203/http://solarsystem.nasa.gov/news/display.cfm?News_ID=36121 |archive-date=June 14, 2011}}</ref>
* '''2005'''&nbsp;– The [[Sloan Digital Sky Survey]] (SDSS) and [[2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey|2dF]] redshift surveys both detected the [[baryon acoustic oscillation]] feature in the galaxy distribution, a key prediction of cold [[dark matter]] models.
* '''2006'''&nbsp;– Three-year [[WMAP]] results are released, confirming previous analysis, correcting several points, and including [[Cosmic microwave background radiation#Polarization|polarization]] data.
* '''2009–2013'''&nbsp;– [[Planck (spacecraft)|Planck]], a space observatory operated by the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA), mapped the anisotropies of the [[cosmic microwave background radiation]], with increased sensitivity and small angular resolution. 
* '''2006–2011'''&nbsp;– Improved measurements from [[WMAP]], new supernova surveys ESSENCE and SNLS, and baryon acoustic oscillations from [[Sloan Digital Sky Survey|SDSS]] and [[Astronomical survey#List of sky surveys|WiggleZ]], continue to be consistent with the standard [[Lambda-CDM model]].
* '''2014'''&nbsp;– Astrophysicists of the [[BICEP and Keck Array|BICEP2]] collaboration announce the detection of inflationary [[gravitational waves]] in the [[B-modes|B-mode]] [[power spectrum]], which if confirmed, would provide clear experimental evidence for the [[Inflation (cosmology)|theory of inflation]].<ref name="BICEP2-2014">{{cite web |author=Staff |title=BICEP2 2014 Results Release |url=http://bicepkeck.org |date=March 17, 2014 |work=[[National Science Foundation]] |access-date=March 18, 2014 }}</ref><ref name="NASA-20140317">{{cite web |last=Clavin |first=Whitney |title=NASA Technology Views Birth of the Universe |url=http://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/news.php?release=2014-082 |date=March 17, 2014 |work=[[NASA]] |access-date=March 17, 2014 }}</ref><ref name="NYT-20140317">{{cite news |last=Overbye |first=Dennis |author-link=Dennis Overbye |title=Space Ripples Reveal Big Bang's Smoking Gun |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/18/science/space/detection-of-waves-in-space-buttresses-landmark-theory-of-big-bang.html |date=March 17, 2014 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=March 17, 2014 }}</ref><ref name="NYT-20140324">{{cite news |last=Overbye |first=Dennis |author-link=Dennis Overbye |title=Ripples From the Big Bang |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/25/science/space/ripples-from-the-big-bang.html |date=March 24, 2014 |work=[[New York Times]] |access-date=March 24, 2014 }}</ref><ref name="PRL-20140619"/><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/?p=6865 | title=BICEP2 News &#124; Not Even Wrong| date=13 May 2014}}</ref> However, in June lowered confidence in confirming the [[cosmic inflation]] findings was reported.<ref name="PRL-20140619">{{cite journal |author=Ade, P.A.R. |author2=BICEP2 Collaboration |title=Detection of B-Mode Polarization at Degree Angular Scales by BICEP2 |date=June 19, 2014 |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=112 |issue=24 |article-number=241101 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.112.241101 |arxiv = 1403.3985 |bibcode = 2014PhRvL.112x1101B |pmid=24996078|s2cid=22780831 }}</ref><ref name="NYT-20140619">{{cite news |last=Overbye |first=Dennis |author-link=Dennis Overbye |title=Astronomers Hedge on Big Bang Detection Claim |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/06/20/science/space/scientists-debate-gravity-wave-detection-claim.html |date=June 19, 2014 |work=[[New York Times]] |access-date=June 20, 2014 }}</ref><ref name="BBC-20140619">{{cite news |last=Amos |first=Jonathan |title=Cosmic inflation: Confidence lowered for Big Bang signal |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-27935479 |date=June 19, 2014 |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=June 20, 2014 }}</ref>
* '''2016'''&nbsp;– [[LIGO Scientific Collaboration]] and [[Virgo interferometer|Virgo Collaboration]] announce that gravitational waves were [[First observation of gravitational waves|directly detected]] by two [[LIGO]] detectors. The [[waveform]] matched the prediction of [[General relativity]] for a gravitational wave emanating from the inward spiral and merger of a pair of [[black hole]]s of around 36 and 29 [[solar mass]]es and the subsequent "ringdown" of the single resulting black hole.<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger|journal = [[Physical Review Letters]]|date = 2016-02-11|issn = 0031-9007|volume = 116|issue = 6|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.061102|language = en|first1 = B. P.|last1 = Abbott|first2 = R.|last2 = Abbott|first3 = T. D.|last3 = Abbott|first4 = M. R.|last4 = Abernathy|first5 = F.|last5 = Acernese|first6 = K.|last6 = Ackley|first7 = C.|last7 = Adams|first8 = T.|last8 = Adams|first9 = P.|last9 = Addesso|arxiv = 1602.03837 |bibcode = 2016PhRvL.116f1102A|pmid=26918975|article-number=061102|s2cid = 124959784}}</ref><ref name="Nature_11Feb16">{{cite journal |title=Einstein's gravitational waves found at last |journal=Nature News |url=http://www.nature.com/news/einstein-s-gravitational-waves-found-at-last-1.19361 |date=11 February 2016 |last1=Castelvecchi |first1=Davide |last2=Witze |first2=Alexandra |doi=10.1038/nature.2016.19361 |s2cid=182916902 |access-date=11 February 2016|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name ="renn">{{cite web |last1=Blum |first1=Alexander |last2=Lalli |first2=Roberto |last3=Renn |first3=Jürgen |author-link3=Jürgen Renn |title=The long road towards evidence |url=http://www.mpg.de/9966773/background |work=[[Max Planck Society]] |date=12 February 2016 |access-date=15 February 2016}}</ref> The [[GW151226|second detection]] verified that GW150914 is not a fluke, thus opens entire new branch in astrophysics, [[gravitational-wave astronomy]].<ref name="PRL-20160615" >{{Cite journal| collaboration=LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration| last=Abbott| first=B. P.| date=15 June 2016| title=GW151226: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a 22-Solar-Mass Binary Black Hole Coalescence| journal=Physical Review Letters| volume= 116| issue= 24| article-number=241103|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.241103| pmid=27367379|arxiv = 1606.04855 |bibcode = 2016PhRvL.116x1103A | s2cid=118651851}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2016/jun/15/ligo-detects-second-black-hole-merger| title=LIGO detects second black-hole merger |date=15 June 2016| first=Tushna| last=Commissariat| website=[[Physics World]]| publisher= [[Institute of Physics]]| access-date=15 June 2016}}</ref>
* '''2019'''&nbsp;– <!--- More informative details could be added here. --->[[Event Horizon Telescope|The Event Horizon Telescope]] Collaboration publishes the image of the black hole at the center of the [[Messier 87|M87 Galaxy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eventhorizontelescope.org/blog/first-ever-image-black-hole-published-event-horizon-telescope-collaboration|title=First-ever Image of a Black Hole Published by the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration|website=eventhorizontelescope.org|date=10 April 2019 |language=en|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref> This is the first time [[astronomer]]s have ever captured an image of a [[black hole]], which once again proves the existence of black holes and thus helps verify [[Albert Einstein|Einstein]]'s [[General relativity|general theory of relativity]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencenews.org/article/black-hole-first-picture-event-horizon-telescope|title=The first picture of a black hole opens a new era of astrophysics|date=2019-04-10|website=Science News|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref> This was done by utilising [[very-long-baseline interferometry]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://skyandtelescope.org/astronomy-blogs/black-hole-files/how-does-very-long-baseline-interferometry-work/|title=How Does the Event Horizon Telescope Work?|date=2019-04-15|website=Sky & Telescope|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-30}}</ref>
* '''2020'''&nbsp;– Physicist [[Lucas Lombriser]] of the [[University of Geneva]] presents a possible way of reconciling the two significantly different determinations of the [[Hubble constant]] by proposing the notion of a surrounding [[Hubble bubble (astronomy)|vast "bubble"]], 250 million light years in diameter, that is half the density of the rest of the universe.<ref name="PHYS-20200310">{{cite news |author=University of Geneva |title=Solved: The mystery of the expansion of the universe |url=https://phys.org/news/2020-03-mystery-expansion-universe.html |date=10 March 2020 |work=[[Phys.org]] |access-date=10 March 2020 |author-link=University of Geneva }}</ref><ref name="PLB-20200410">{{cite journal |last=Lombriser |first=Lucas |title=Consistency of the local Hubble constant with the cosmic microwave background |date=10 April 2020 |journal=[[Physics Letters B]] |volume=803 |article-number=135303 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2020.135303 |arxiv=1906.12347 |bibcode=2020PhLB..80335303L |s2cid=195750638 }}</ref>
* '''2020'''&nbsp;– Scientists publish a study which suggests that the Universe is no longer [[Expansion of the Universe|expanding]] at the same rate in all directions and that therefore the widely accepted [[Isotropy#Cosmology|isotropy hypothesis]] might be wrong. While previous studies already suggested this, the study is the first to examine [[galaxy cluster]]s in X-rays and, according to Norbert Schartel, has a much greater significance. The study found a consistent and strong directional behavior of [[Hubble's law#Measured values of the Hubble constant|deviations – which have earlier been described to indicate a "crisis of cosmology" by others – of the normalization parameter A, or the Hubble constant H0]]. Beyond the potential [[cosmological]] implications, it shows that studies which assume perfect isotropy in the properties of galaxy clusters and their scaling relations can produce strongly biased results.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rethinking cosmology: Universe expansion may not be uniform (Update) |url=https://phys.org/news/2020-04-basic-assumption-universe.html |website=phys.org |access-date=15 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Nasa study challenges one of our most basic ideas about the universe |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/universe-expanding-direction-nasa-esa-cosmology-isotropic-a9455641.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/universe-expanding-direction-nasa-esa-cosmology-isotropic-a9455641.html |archive-date=2022-05-07 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=23 May 2020 |work=The Independent |date=8 April 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Parts of the universe may be expanding faster than others |url=https://newatlas.com/physics/universe-expansion-not-uniform/ |access-date=23 May 2020 |work=New Atlas |date=9 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Doubts about basic assumption for the universe |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-04/uob-dab040820.php |access-date=23 May 2020 |work=EurekAlert! |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Migkas |first1=K. |last2=Schellenberger |first2=G. |last3=Reiprich |first3=T. H. |last4=Pacaud |first4=F. |last5=Ramos-Ceja |first5=M. E. |last6=Lovisari |first6=L. |title=Probing cosmic isotropy with a new X-ray galaxy cluster sample through the LX–T scaling relation |journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics |date=8 April 2020 |volume=636 |pages=A15 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201936602  |doi-access=free|arxiv=2004.03305 |bibcode=2020A&A...636A..15M |s2cid=215238834 |url=https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/abs/2020/04/aa36602-19/aa36602-19.html |access-date=15 May 2020 |language=en |issn=0004-6361}}</ref>
* '''2020'''&nbsp;– Scientists report verifying measurements 2011–2014 via [[ULAS J1120+0641]] of what seem to be [[fine-structure constant#Potential time-variation|a spatial variation in four measurements of the fine-structure constant]], a basic physical constant used to measure [[electromagnetism]] between charged particles, which indicates that there might be directionality with varying natural constants in the Universe which would have implications for [[Physical constant#Fine-tuned universe|theories on the emergence of habitability of the Universe]] and be at odds with the widely accepted theory of constant [[natural law]]s and the standard model of [[cosmology]] which is based on an [[Isotropy|isotropic]] Universe.<ref>{{cite news |title=The laws of physics may break down at the edge of the universe |url=https://futurism.com/the-byte/laws-physics-break-down-edge-universe |access-date=17 May 2020 |work=Futurism |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=New findings suggest laws of nature 'downright weird,' not as constant as previously thought |url=https://phys.org/news/2020-04-laws-nature-downright-weird-constant.html |access-date=17 May 2020 |work=phys.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name="SA-20200428">{{cite news |last=Field |first=David |title=New Tests Suggest a Fundamental Constant of Physics Isn't The Same Across The Universe |url=https://www.sciencealert.com/new-tests-suggest-the-fundamental-forces-of-nature-aren-t-constant-across-the-universe |date=28 April 2020 |work=ScienceAlert.com |access-date=29 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wilczynska |first1=Michael R. |last2=Webb |first2=John K. |last3=Bainbridge |first3=Matthew |last4=Barrow |first4=John D. |last5=Bosman |first5=Sarah E. I. |last6=Carswell |first6=Robert F. |last7=Dąbrowski |first7=Mariusz P. |last8=Dumont |first8=Vincent |last9=Lee |first9=Chung-Chi |last10=Leite |first10=Ana Catarina |last11=Leszczyńska |first11=Katarzyna |last12=Liske |first12=Jochen |last13=Marosek |first13=Konrad |last14=Martins |first14=Carlos J. A. P. |last15=Milaković |first15=Dinko |last16=Molaro |first16=Paolo |last17=Pasquini |first17=Luca |title=Four direct measurements of the fine-structure constant 13 billion years ago |journal=Science Advances |date=1 April 2020 |volume=6 |issue=17 |article-number=eaay9672 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.aay9672 |pmc=7182409  |pmid=32426462 |arxiv=2003.07627 |bibcode=2020SciA....6.9672W |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* '''2021'''&nbsp;– [[James Webb Space Telescope]] is launched.<ref name="AS-20211225">{{cite press release |url=https://www.arianespace.com/press-release/ariane-5-successful-launch-webb-space-telescope/ |title=Ariane 5 goes down in history with successful launch of Webb |work=[[Arianespace]] |date=25 December 2021 |access-date=25 December 2021 |archive-date=10 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220310095539/https://www.arianespace.com/press-release/ariane-5-successful-launch-webb-space-telescope/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* '''2022-2025 – JWST breaks the timeline:''' JWST was built to find first galaxies. It found them ''too early, too big, too developed''. Galaxies at $z > 10$ (<500 Myr after Big Bang) with stellar masses comparable to the Milky Way today. The standard model predicted thin infant galaxies at that epoch; JWST sent back adults in the nursery. UV-bright galaxies at $z \gtrsim 10$ and massive galaxies at $z \gtrsim 7$ challenge standard galaxy formation in ΛCDM.

[[File:E mc 2 IMG 0859.jpg|thumb|Einstein's mass-energy equation in a 1912 manuscript. He originally used <math>L</math> instead of <math>E</math> to denote energy.|260x260px]]
{{General relativity sidebar}}
The following is a '''[[timeline]] of [[gravitational physics]] and [[general relativity]]'''.

==Before 1500==
* 3rd century B.C. – [[Aristarchus of Samos]] proposes the [[Heliocentrism|heliocentric model]].<ref name=":9">{{Cite book |last=Bauer |first=Susan Wise |title=The Story of Science from the Writings of Aristotle to the Big Bang Theory |publisher=W. W. Norton & Company |year=2015 |isbn=978-0-393-24326-0 |location=New York |chapter=Chapter Seven: The Last Ancient Astronomer |author-link=Susan Wise Bauer}}</ref>

==1500s==
* 1543 – [[Nicolaus Copernicus]] publishes [[De revolutionibus orbium coelestium|''On the Revolutions of Heavenly Spheres'']].<ref name=":9" />
* 1583 – [[Galileo Galilei]] deduces the period relationship of a [[pendulum]] from observations (according to later biographer).
* 1586 – [[Simon Stevin]] demonstrates that two objects of different masses accelerate at the same rate when dropped.<ref name=":21" />{{Reference page|pages=76-7}}
* 1589 – Galileo Galilei describes a [[hydrostatic balance]] for measuring [[specific gravity]].
* 1590 – Galileo Galilei formulates modified [[Aristotle|Aristotelian]] theory  of motion (later retracted) based on [[density]] rather than weight of objects.

==1600s==
[[File:Principia1846-105.png|thumb|Geometric diagram for Newton's proof of Kepler's second law.]]
* 1602-1608 – Galileo Galilei experiments with pendulum motion and [[inclined plane]]s; deduces his law of [[free fall]]; and discovers that [[projectile]]s travel along [[Parabola|parabolic]] trajectories.<ref name=":11">{{Cite book |last1=Pasachoff |first1=Naomi |title=The Scientists: An Epic of Discovery |last2=Pasachoff |first2=Jay |publisher=Thames and Hudson |year=2012 |isbn=978-0-500-25191-1 |editor-last=Robinson |editor-first=Andrew |location=New York |chapter=Galileo Galilei}}</ref>
* 1609 – [[Johannes Kepler]] announces his first two [[Kepler's laws of planetary motion|laws of planetary motion]].<ref name=":8">{{Cite book |last=Dolnick |first=Edward |title=The Clockwork Universe: Isaac Newton, the Royal Society, and the Birth of the Modern World |publisher=Harper Collins |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-06-171951-6 |location=New York |chapter=Timeline}}</ref>
* 1610 – Johannes Kepler states the [[Olbers's paradox|dark night paradox]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olber's Paradox: Why Is The Sky Dark at Night? |url=https://www.amnh.org/exhibitions/journey-to-the-stars/educator-resources/stars/olbers-paradox |access-date=June 6, 2024 |website=American Museum of Natural History}}</ref>
* 1610 – Galileo Galilei publishes ''[[Sidereus Nuncius|The Sidereal Messenger]]'', detailing his astronomical discoveries made with a telescope.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bauer |first=Susan Wise |title=The Story of Science: From the Writings of Aristotle to the Big Bang Theory |publisher=W. W. Norton & Company |year=2015 |isbn=978-0-393-24326-0 |location=New York |chapter=Chapter Ten: The Death of Aristotle}}</ref>
* 1619 – Johannes Kepler unveils his third law of planetary motion.<ref name=":8" />
* 1665-66 – [[Isaac Newton]] introduces an inverse-square [[Newton's law of universal gravitation|law of universal gravitation]] uniting terrestrial and celestial theories of motion and uses it to predict the orbit of the [[Moon]] and the parabolic arc of projectiles (the latter using his [[Binomial series|generalization of the binomial theorem]]).<ref name=":10">{{Cite book |last=Iliffe |first=Rob |title=The Scientists: An Epic of Discovery |publisher=Thames and Hudson |year=2012 |isbn=978-0-500-25191-1 |editor-last=Robinson |editor-first=Andrew |location=New York |chapter=Isaac Newton}}</ref>
* 1673 – [[Christiaan Huygens]] publishes his ''[[Horologium Oscillatorium|The Pendulum Clock]]'', describing the motion of [[pendulum]]s and the formula for centripetal acceleration during [[Circular motion#Uniform circular motion|uniform circular motion]], known to Isaac Newton since the 1660s.<ref name=":18" />{{Reference page|page=14}}
* 1676-9 – [[Ole Rømer]] makes the first scientific determination of the [[speed of light]].<ref name=":21">{{Cite book |last=Gribbin|first=John|title=The Scientists: A History of Science Told Through the Lives of Its Greatest Inventors|publisher=Random House|year=2004|isbn=978-0-812-96788-3|location=New York|pages=|chapter=|author-link=John Gribbin}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=122-3}}
* 1684 – Isaac Newton proves that [[planet]]s moving under an inverse-square force law will obey [[Kepler's laws]] in [[De motu corporum in gyrum|a letter]] to Edmond Halley.<ref name=":10" />
* 1686 – Isaac Newton uses a fixed length pendulum with weights of varying composition to test the [[weak equivalence principle]] to 1 part in 1000.<ref name=":7">{{Cite book |last=Newton |first=Isaac |title=The Principia: The Authoritative Translation and Guide |publisher=University of California Press |year=1999 |isbn=978-0-520-29088-4 |translator-last=Cohen |translator-first=I. Bernard |translator-last2=Whitman |translator-first2=Anne |translator-last3=Budenz |translator-first3=Julia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Kleppner |first1=Daniel |title=[[An Introduction to Mechanics]] |last2=Kolenkow |first2=Robert J. |publisher=McGraw-Hill |year=1973 |isbn=0-07-035048-5 |publication-date=1973 |pages= |chapter=|edition=1st|author-link=Robert J. Kolenkow|author-link2=Daniel Kleppner}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=353-4}}
* 1686 – Isaac Newton publishes his ''[[Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica|Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy]]'', where he develops his [[Fluxion|calculus]], states his [[Newton's laws of motion|laws of motion]] and gravitation, proves the [[shell theorem]], describes his [[Bucket argument|rotating bucket]] thought experiment, explains the [[Tidal force|tides]], and calculates the [[figure of the Earth]].<ref name=":7" />
* 1692 – [[Richard Bentley]] states his [[Bentley's paradox|cosmological paradox]] in a letter to Newton.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kaku |first=Michio |title=Physics of the Impossible: A Scientific Exploration Into the World of Phasers, Force Fields, Teleportation, and Time Travel |publisher=Doubleday |year=2008 |isbn=978-0-385-52069-0 |location=New York}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=292}}

==1700s==
* 1705 – [[Edmond Halley]] predicts the return of [[Halley's Comet|Halley's comet]] in 1758,<ref>{{cite book |last=Halley |first=Edmund |url=https://archive.org/details/synopsisofastron00hall/page/n3/mode/2up |title=A synopsis of the astronomy of comets |publisher=John Senex |year=1705 |place=Oxford |access-date=16 June 2020 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref> the first use of Newton's laws by someone other than Newton himself.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Sagan |first1=Carl |title=Comet |last2=Druyan |first2=Ann |publisher=Random House |year=1997 |isbn=978-0-3078-0105-0 |location=New York |pages=66–67}}</ref>
* 1728 – Isaac Newton posthumously publishes his [[Newton's cannonball|cannonball]] thought experiment.<ref name="treatiselat">[https://books.google.com/books?id=ewhgAAAAcAAJ ''De mundi systemate''], Isaac Newton, London: J. Tonson, J. Osborn, & T. Longman, 1728.</ref><ref name="cohen2004">{{Cite book |last1=Newton |first1=Isaac |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UvyPx-DwnrAC |title=A Treatise of the System of the World |last2=Cohen |first2=I. Bernard |date=2004-01-01 |publisher=Courier Corporation |isbn=978-0-486-43880-1 |language=en}}</ref>
* 1730s – [[Alexis Clairaut|Alexis Clairault]] examines [[equipotential]] surfaces and develops the notions of [[Partial derivative|partial differentiation]] and [[Exact differential|exact differentials]].<ref name=":24">{{Cite journal |last=Grattan-Guinness|first=Ivor|author-link=Ivor Grattan-Guinness|date=May 1995|title=Why Did George Green Write His Essay of 1828 on Electricity and Magnetism?|journal=[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=102|issue=5|pages=387–96|doi=10.1080/00029890.1995.12004591}}</ref>
* 1742 – [[Colin Maclaurin]] studies a self-gravitating uniform liquid drop at [[Hydrostatic equilibrium|equilibrium]], the [[Maclaurin spheroid]].<ref>Maclaurin, Colin. A Treatise of Fluxions: In Two Books. 1. Vol. 1. Ruddimans, 1742.</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Chandrasekhar |first=Subrahmanyan |title=Ellipsoidal Figures of Equilibrium |publisher=Yale University Press |year=1969 |isbn=978-0-30001-116-6 |location=New Haven |chapter=5: The Maclaurin Spheroids}}</ref>
* 1740s – [[Jean le Rond d'Alembert]] and [[Leonhard Euler]] independently examine the [[Axial precession|precession of the equinoxes]] and [[nutation]] of the Earth. In the process, they develop the dynamics of [[Rigid body|rigid bodies]].<ref name=":16">{{Cite book |last=Wilson |first=Curtis |title=The Cambridge Companion to Newton |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2002 |isbn=0-521-65696-6 |editor-last=Cohen |editor-first=I. Bernard |chapter=Newton and Celestial Mechanics |editor-last2=Smith |editor-first2=George|editor-link=I. Bernard Cohen|editor-link2=George E. Smith (philosopher)}}</ref>
* 1740s-1750s – Leonhard Euler and Alexis Clairault independently derive the equations of motion for the [[three-body problem]] and apply them to the Moon.<ref name=":16" />
* 1755 – [[Immanuel Kant]] advances [[Emanuel Swedenborg]]'s nebular hypothesis on the origin of the [[Solar System]].<ref name="Woolfson1993">{{cite journal |last=Woolfson |first=M.M. |date=1993 |title=Solar System&nbsp;– its origin and evolution |journal=Q. J. R. Astron. Soc. |volume=34 |pages=1–20 |bibcode=1993QJRAS..34....1W}} For details of Kant's position, see Stephen Palmquist, "Kant's Cosmogony Re-Evaluated", ''Studies in History and Philosophy of Science'' 18:3 (September 1987), pp.255–269.</ref>
[[File:Lagrange very massive.svg|thumb|Lagrange points]]
* 1765 – Leonhard Euler discovers the first three Lagrange points.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Koon |first1=W. S. |url=http://www.cds.caltech.edu/~marsden/books/Mission_Design.html |title=Dynamical Systems, the Three-Body Problem, and Space Mission Design |last2=Lo |first2=M. W. |last3=Marsden |first3=J. E. |last4=Ross |first4=S. D. |date=2006 |page=9 |access-date=2008-06-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080527145955/http://www.cds.caltech.edu/~marsden/books/Mission_Design.html |archive-date=2008-05-27 }} (16MB)</ref><ref name="E327">{{cite book |last=Euler |first=Leonhard |url=https://www.math.dartmouth.edu/~euler/docs/originals/E327.pdf |title=De motu rectilineo trium corporum se mutuo attrahentium |date=1765 |author-link=Leonhard Euler}}</ref>
* 1767 – Leonhard Euler solves Euler's [[Euler's three-body problem|restricted three-body problem]].<ref name="euler_1760">[[Leonhard Euler|Euler L]], ''Nov. Comm. Acad. Imp. Petropolitanae'', '''10''', pp. 207–242, '''11''', pp. 152–184; ''Mémoires de l'Acad. de Berlin'', '''11''', 228–249.</ref>
* 1772 – [[Joseph-Louis Lagrange]] discovers the two remaining [[Lagrange point]]s.<ref name="gallica.bnf.fr2">{{Cite book |last=Lagrange |first=Joseph-Louis |title=Œuvres de Lagrange |date=1867–92 |publisher=Gauthier-Villars |pages=229–334 |language=fr |chapter=Tome 6, Chapitre II: Essai sur le problème des trois corps |author-link=Joseph-Louis Lagrange |chapter-url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k229225j/f231.image.r=Oeuvres+de+Lagrange.langFR}}</ref>
* 1770s – [[Pierre-Simon de Laplace]] develops [[Theory of tides#Laplace's tidal equations|equations for the tides]] that take into account both gravitation and rotation.<ref name=":18">{{Cite book |last=Cohen |first=I. Bernard |author-link=I. Bernard Cohen |title=A Guide to Newton's ''Principia'' |publisher=University of California Press |year=1999 |isbn=978-0-520-08817-7}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=216}}
* 1770s-1780s – Joseph-Louis Lagrange and Pierre-Simon de Laplace investigate the stability of the Solar System.<ref name=":16" />
* 1780s – [[Adrien-Marie Legendre]] and Pierre-Simon de Laplace study the gravitational attraction of [[spheroid]]s in [[Spherical coordinate system|spherical coordinates]] and introduce the [[Legendre polynomials]].<ref name=":16" />
* 1781 – [[William Herschel]] discovers the planet [[Uranus]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kuhn |first=Thomas S. |author-link=Thomas Kuhn |title=The Structure of Scientific Revolutions |publisher=University of Chicago Press |year=2012 |isbn=978-0-226-45812-0 |edition=50th Anniversary |orig-date=1962}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=115-6}}
* 1783 – [[John Michell]] speculates that a star could be so massive that its gravitational field would prevent light from escaping.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Refrigerator and the Universe: Understanding the Laws of Energy|last1=Goldstein|first1=Martin|publisher=Harvard University Press|year=1993|isbn=0-674-75324-0|location=Cambridge, Massachusetts|last2=Goldstein|first2=Inge F.}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=372}} Pierre-Simon de Laplace proposes the same thing in 1795.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=537}}
* 1796 – Pierre-Simon de Laplace independently introduces the [[nebular hypothesis]].<ref name="Woolfson1993" />
* 1798 – [[Henry Cavendish]] tests Newton's law of universal gravitation using a [[Cavendish experiment|torsion balance]], leading to the first accurate value for the [[gravitational constant]] and the mean density of the Earth.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Cavendish |first=Henry |year=1798 |title=Experiments to Determine the Density of Earth |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society |volume=88 |pages=469–526 |doi=10.1098/rstl.1798.0022 |jstor=106988 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Clotfelter |first1=B.E. |year=1987 |title=The Cavendish Experiment as Cavendish Knew It |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=55 |issue=3 |pages=210–213 |bibcode=1987AmJPh..55..210C |doi=10.1119/1.15214}}</ref>
* 1799-1825 – Pierre-Simon de Laplace publishes his ''[[Traité de mécanique céleste|Treatise on Celestial Mechanics]]'', in five volumes.<ref name=":18" />{{Reference page|page=216}}

==1800s==
* 1846 – [[Urbain Le Verrier]] and [[John Couch Adams]] independently show that the orbit of [[Uranus]] is perturbed by another planet, [[Neptune]], promptly discovered by [[Johann Gottfried Galle]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Eisenstaedt|first=Jean|title=The Curious History of Relativity: How Einstein's Theory of Gravity Was Lost and Found Again|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2006|isbn=978-0-691-11865-9|location=Princeton, NJ|translator-last=Sangalli|translator-first=Arturo}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=151-2}}
* 1849 – [[Hippolyte Fizeau|Armand Fizeau]] makes the first terrestrial determination of the speed of light.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Optics|last=Hecht|first=Eugene|publisher=Pearson|year=2017|isbn=978-0-133-97722-6|edition=5th|author-link=Eugene Hecht}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=5}}
* 1855 – Le Verrier observes a 38 [[Arcsecond|arc-second]] per century excess [[precession]] of [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]]'s [[orbit]] and attributes it to another planet, inside Mercury's orbit. The planet, called [[Vulcan (hypothetical planet)|Vulcan]], was never found. Le Verrier's figure is revised by [[Simon Newcomb]] to 43 arc-second per century in 1882.<ref name=":16" />
* 1876 – [[William Kingdon Clifford]] suggests that the motion of matter may be due to changes in the geometry of space.<ref>[[s:On the Space Theory of Matter]]</ref>
* 1880 – [[Aurel Voss]] discovers the [[contracted Bianchi identities]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Voss |first=Aurel |date=1880 |title=Zur Theorie der Transformation quadratischer Differentialausdrücke und der Krümmung höherer Mannigfaltigkeiten |trans-title=On the theory of the transformation of quadratic differential expressions and the curvature of higher manifolds |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01446384 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=German |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=129–179 |doi=10.1007/BF01446384}}</ref> subsequently rediscovered independently by [[Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro]] in 1889 and [[Luigi Bianchi]] in 1902.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bianchi |first=Luigi |date=1902 |title=Sui simboli a quattro indici e sulla curvatura di Riemann |trans-title=On Four-Index Symbols and Riemann Curvature |journal=Rend. Acc. Naz. Lincei |language=Italian |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=3–7}}</ref><ref name=":03" />{{Reference page|pages=275-6}}
* 1884 – William Thomson ([[Lord Kelvin]]) lectures on the issues with the wave theory of light with regards to the [[Luminiferous aether|luminiferous ether]].<ref name=":15" />
* 1887 – [[Albert A. Michelson]] and [[Edward W. Morley]] report a [[null result]] in [[Michelson–Morley experiment|their experiment]] to detect the ether drift.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Michaelson |first1=Albert A. |last2=Morley |first2=Edward W. |date=1887 |title=On the Relative Motion of the Earth and the Luminiferous Ether |url=https://ajs.scholasticahq.com/article/62505 |journal=American Journal of Science |volume=134 |issue=333 |pages=333–345 |doi=10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333|bibcode=1887AmJS...34..333M |s2cid=124333204 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=French|first=A. P.|title=Special Relativity|publisher=W. W. Norton & Company|year=1968|isbn=0-393-09793-5|location=New York|pages=|chapter=|author-link=Anthony Philip French}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=52-8}}
* 1888 – [[Oliver Heaviside]] calculates the electromagnetic field of a moving point charge at constant velocity,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jefimenko |first=Oleg |author-link=Oleg Jefimenko |date=1994 |title=Direct calculation of the electric and magnetic fields of an electric point charge moving with constant velocity |url=https://pubs.aip.org/aapt/ajp/article-abstract/62/1/79/1054440/Direct-calculation-of-the-electric-and-magnetic |journal=[[American Journal of Physics]] |volume=62 |issue=1 |pages=79–85 |doi=10.1119/1.17716|bibcode=1994AmJPh..62...79J |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and realizes, with some help by [[George Frederick Charles Searle]], that the field contracts in the direction of motion.<ref name=":32">{{Cite book |last=Mahon|first=Basil|title=The Forgotten Genius of Oliver Heaviside: A Maverick of Electrical Science|publisher=[[Prometheus Books]]|year=2017|isbn=978-1-63388-331-4}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=181}}
* 1889 – [[Loránd Eötvös]] uses a [[Torsion spring#Torsion balance|torsion balance]] to test the [[weak equivalence principle]] to 1 part in one billion.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bod |first1=L. |last2=Fischbach |first2=E. |last3=Marx |first3=G. |last4=Náray-Ziegler |first4=Maria |date=31 Aug 1990 |title=One Hundred Years of the Eötvös Experiment |url=http://www.kfki.hu/eotvos/onehund.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022054838/http://www.kfki.hu/eotvos/onehund.html |archive-date=October 22, 2012}}</ref>
* 1892 – [[George Francis FitzGerald]] explains his hypothesis that the Michelson-Morley interferometer [[Fitzgerald-Lorentz contraction|contracts]] in the direction of motion through the [[Luminiferous aether|luminiferous ether]] to [[Oliver Lodge]].<ref name=":15">{{Cite journal |last=Shankland |first=Robert Sherwood |author-link=Robert Sherwood Shankland |date=1964 |title=Michelson-Morley Experiment |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=32 |issue=1 |pages=16–35 |doi=10.1119/1.1970063 |bibcode=1964AmJPh..32...16S }}</ref>
* 1893 – [[Ernst Mach]] states [[Mach's principle]], the first constructive critique of the idea of Newtonian absolute space.
* 1897 – [[Henri Poincaré]] questions whether absolute space, absolute time, and [[Euclidean geometry]] are applicable to physics.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Isaacson |first=Walter |author-link=Walter Isaacson |title=Einstein: His Life and Universe |publisher=[[Simon & Schuster]] |year=2007 |page=37 |chapter=Chapter Three: The Zurich Polytechnic}}</ref>

==1900s==
[[File:USS_Enterprise_(CVAN-65),_USS_Long_Beach_(CGN-9)_and_USS_Bainbridge_(DLGN-25)_underway_in_the_Mediterranean_Sea_during_Operation_Sea_Orbit,_in_1964.jpg|right|thumb|The U.S. Navy's nuclear-powered Task Force 1 underway for [[Operation Sea Orbit]] in the Mediterranean, 1964, while displaying Einstein's mass-energy equation.]]
* 1902 – [[Paul Gerber]] explains the movement of the perihelion of Mercury using finite [[speed of gravity]].<ref>{{Cite journal
|author=Gerber, P.
|orig-date=1902|year=1917
|title=Die Fortpflanzungsgeschwindigkeit der Gravitation
|journal=Annalen der Physik
|volume=52
|pages =415–444
|doi=10.1002/andp.19173570404
|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k153544.image.f425
|issue=4|bibcode = 1917AnP...357..415G }} (Originally published in Programmabhandlung des städtischen Realgymnasiums zu Stargard i. Pomm., 1902)</ref> His formula, at least approximately, matches the later model from Einstein's general relativity, but Gerber's theory was incorrect.
* 1902 – Henri Poincaré questions the concept of [[Relativity of simultaneity|simultaneity]] in his book, ''[[Science and Hypothesis]]''.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=Robinson |first=Andrew |title=The Scientists: An Epic of Discovery |publisher=Thames and Hudson |year=2012 |isbn=978-0-500-25191-1 |editor-last=Robinson |editor-first=Andrew |location=New York |chapter=Albert Einstein}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Galison |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Galison |title=The Universe |publisher=HarperCollins |year=2014 |isbn=978-0-06-229608-5 |editor-last=Brockman |editor-first=John |editor-link=John Brockman (literary agent) |location=New York |chapter=Einstein and Poincaré}}</ref>
* 1904 – [[Hendrik Antoon Lorentz]] publishes the [[Lorentz transformation]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lorentz |first=Hendrik Antoon |date=1904 |title=Electromagnetic Phenomena in a System Moving with Any Velocity Smaller than That of Light |url=https://www.dwc.knaw.nl/DL/publications/PU00014148.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |volume=6 |pages=809–831}}</ref> so named by Henri Poincaré.<ref name=":15" />
* 1902 – Henri Poincaré shows that the Lorentz transformations form a [[Group (mathematics)|mathematical group]], called the [[Lorentz group]], and derives the [[Velocity-addition formula|relativistic formula for adding velocities]].<ref name=":15" />
* 1905 – [[Albert Einstein]] completes his [[special relativity|special theory of relativity]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1905 |title=Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper |trans-title=On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies |url=https://www.physik.uni-augsburg.de/annalen/history/einstein-papers/1905_17_891-921.pdf |journal=Annalen der Physik |series=Series 4 |volume=17 |issue=10 |pages=891–921|doi=10.1002/andp.19053221004 |bibcode=1905AnP...322..891E }}</ref><ref name=":82">{{Cite book |last=Isaacson |first=Walter |title=Einstein: His Life and Universe |publisher=[[Simon & Schuster]] |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-7432-6473-0 |location=New York |chapter=Chapter Six: Special Relativity}}</ref> and examines [[relativistic aberration]] and the [[transverse Doppler effect]].<ref name=":15" />
* 1905 – Albert Einstein discovers the [[Mass–energy equivalence|equivalence of mass and energy]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1905 |title=Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig? |trans-title=Does the Inertia of a Body Depend upon its Energy Content? |url=https://www.physik.uni-augsburg.de/annalen/history/einstein-papers/1905_18_639-641.pdf |journal=Annalen der Physik |series=Series 4 |volume=18 |issue=13 |pages=639–641|doi=10.1002/andp.19053231314 |bibcode=1905AnP...323..639E |s2cid=122309633 }}</ref> <math>E = mc^2</math> in modern form.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1935 |title=Elementary derivation of the equivalence of mass and energy |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2000-37-01/S0273-0979-99-00805-8/S0273-0979-99-00805-8.pdf |journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=223–230 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1935-06046-X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hecht |first=Eugene |author-link=Eugene Hecht |date=2011 |title=How Einstein Confirmed <math>E_0 = m c^2</math> |url=https://pubs.aip.org/aapt/ajp/article-abstract/79/6/591/1041052/How-Einstein-confirmed-E0-mc2 |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=79 |pages=591–600 |doi=10.1119/1.3549223|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":12" /> He notes that it may be tested using [[Radioactive decay|radioactive]] substances.<ref name=":03" />{{Reference page|page=149}} He returns to the problem multiple times later.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ohanian |first=Hans |date=May 2009 |title=Did Einstein prove <math> E = mc^2 </math>? |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1355219809000112#bib21 |journal=Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part B |volume=40 |issue=2 |pages=167–173 |doi=10.1016/j.shpsb.2009.03.002|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hecht |first=Eugene |author-link=Eugene Hecht |date=June 2011 |title=How Einstein Confirmed <math>E_0=mc^2</math> |url=https://pubs.aip.org/aapt/ajp/article-abstract/79/6/591/1041052/How-Einstein-confirmed-E0-mc2 |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=79 |issue=6 |pages=591–600 |doi=10.1119/1.3549223|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":03">{{cite book |last=Pais |first=Abraham |author-link=Abraham Pais |title='Subtle is the Lord..': The Science and the Life of Albert Einstein |title-link=Subtle is the Lord |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=1982 |isbn=0-19-853907-X |location=Oxford |pages=}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=154}}
* 1906 – [[Max Planck]] coins the term ''Relativtheorie''. Albert Einstein later uses the term ''Relativitätstheorie'' in a conversation with Paul Ehrenfest. He originally prefers calling it Invariance Theory.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Isaacson |first=Walter |author-link=Walter Isaacson |title=Einstein: His Life and Universe |publisher=[[Simon & Schuster]] |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-7432-6473-0 |page=132 |chapter=Chapter Six: Special Relativity}}</ref>
* 1906 – Max Planck discovers the [[Energy–momentum relation|energy-momentum relation]] and formulates a [[variational principle]] for special relativity.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Planck, Max |year=1906 |title=Das Prinzip der Relativität und die Grundgleichungen der Mechanik |trans-title=The Principle of Relativity and the Fundamental Equations of Mechanics |url=https://archive.org/details/verhandlungende00goog/page/n179 |journal=Verhandlungen der Deutschen Physikalischen Gesellschaft |volume=8 |issue=7 |pages=136–141}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Isaacson |first=Walter |author-link=Walter Isaacson |title=Einstein: His Life and Universe |publisher=[[Simon & Schuster]] |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-7432-6473-0 |page=141 |chapter=Chapter Seven: The Happiest Thought}}</ref>
* 1907 – Albert Einstein introduces the [[Equivalence principle|principle of equivalence]] of gravitational and inertial mass and uses it to predict gravitational lensing and [[gravitational redshift]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1907 |title=Relativitätsprinzip und die aus demselben gezogenen Folgerungen |trans-title=On the Relativity Principle and the Conclusions Drawn from It |url=https://www.soso.ch/wissen/hist/SRT/E-1907.pdf |journal=Jahrbuch der Radioaktivität |issue=4 |pages=411–462}}</ref><ref name=":22">{{Cite book |last1=McEvoy |first1=J. P. |title=Introducing Stephen Hawking |last2=Zarate |first2=Oscar |publisher=Totem Books |year=1995 |isbn=978-1-874-16625-2}}</ref> historically known as the Einstein shift.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Eddington |first=A. S. |date=1926 |title=Einstein Shift and Doppler Shift |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=117 |issue=2933 |page=86 |bibcode=1926Natur.117...86E |doi=10.1038/117086a0 |issn=1476-4687 |s2cid=4092843 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1907-8 – [[Hermann Minkowski]] introduces the [[Minkowski spacetime]] and expresses [[Electromagnetic tensor|electromagnetic field strengths]] as a second-rank [[tensor]]. He also coins the terms ''spacelike'', ''timelike'', ''[[light cone]]'', and ''[[world line]]''.<ref name=":03" />{{Reference page|pages=151-2}} His paper is published posthumously.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Minkowski |first=Hermann |date=1915 |title=Das Relativitätsprinzip |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/andp.19153521505 |journal=Annalen der Physik |volume=352 |issue=15 |pages=927–938 |doi=10.1002/andp.19153521505|bibcode=1915AnP...352..927M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Corry |first=Leo |date=1997 |title=Hermann Minkowski and the Postulate of Relativity |url=https://www.tau.ac.il/~corry/publications/articles/pdf/mink.pdf |journal=Archive for History of Exact Sciences |volume=51 |issue=4 |pages=273–314 |doi=10.1007/BF00518231|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-002A-737E-6 |s2cid=27016039 }}</ref><ref name=":21" />{{Reference page|pages=440-1}}
* 1909 – [[Max Born]] proposes [[Born rigidity|his notion of rigidity]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Born |first=Max |date=1909 |title=Die Theorie des starren Elektrons in der Kinematik des Relativitätsprinzips |trans-title=The theory of the rigid electron in the kinematics of the principle of relativity |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/andp.19093351102 |journal=Annalen der Physik |language=German |volume=355 |issue=11 |pages=1–56 |doi=10.1002/andp.19093351102|bibcode=1909AnP...335....1B }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Born |first=Max |date=1909 |title=Über die Dynamik des Elektrons in der Kinematik des Relativitätsprinzips |journal=Physikalische Zeitschrift |volume=10 |pages=814–17}}</ref>
* 1909 – [[Paul Ehrenfest]] states the [[Ehrenfest paradox]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehrenfest |first=Paul |date=1909 |title=Gleichförmige Rotation starrer Körper und Relativitätstheorie |trans-title=Uniform Rotation of Rigid Bodies and Theory of Relativity |journal=Physikalische Zeitschrift |language=German |volume=10 |issue=918 |page=918 |bibcode=1909PhyZ...10..918E}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weber |first=T. A. |date=1997 |title=A note on rotating coordinates in relativity |url=https://pubs.aip.org/aapt/ajp/article-abstract/65/6/486/530041/A-note-on-rotating-coordinates-in-relativity |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=65 |issue=6 |pages=486–7 |doi=10.1119/1.18575|bibcode=1997AmJPh..65..486W |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== 1910s ===
[[File:Einstein's_argument_that_falling_light_acquires_energy.svg|thumb|Einstein's 1911 argument for gravitational redshift]]
* 1911 – [[Max von Laue]] publishes the first textbook on special relativity.<ref name=":14">{{Cite journal |last1=Janssen |first1=Michel |last2=Renn |first2=Jürgen |author-link2=Jürgen Renn |date=November 2015 |title=History: Einstein Was No Lone Genius |journal=Nature |volume=527 |issue=7578 |pages=298–300 |doi=10.1038/527298a |pmid=26581276 |bibcode=2015Natur.527..298J }}</ref>
* 1911 – Albert Einstein explains the need to replace both special relativity and Newton's theory of gravity; he realizes that the principle of equivalence only holds locally, not globally.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1911 |title=Einfluss der Schwerkraft auf die Ausbreitung des Lichtes |trans-title=On the Influence of Gravitation upon the Propagation of Light |url=https://www.physik.uni-augsburg.de/annalen/history/einstein-papers/1911_35_898-908.pdf |journal=Annalen der Physik |series=Series 4 |language=German |volume=35 |pages=898–908|doi=10.1002/andp.19113401005 }}</ref>
* 1912 – [[Friedrich Kottler]] applies the notion of tensors to curved spacetime.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kottler |first=Friedrich |date=1912 |title=Über die Raumzeitlinien der Minkowski'schen Welt |trans-title=On the Spacetime Lines of a Minkowski World |journal=Wiener Sitzungsberichte 2a |language=German |volume=121 |pages=1659–1759}}</ref><ref name=":14" />
* 1915-16 – Albert Einstein completes his [[General relativity|general theory of relativity]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1915 |title=Feldgleichungen der Gravitation |trans-title=Field Equations of Gravitation |journal=Preussische Akademie der Wissenschaften, Sitzungsberichte |pages=844–847}}</ref><ref name=":13">{{Cite journal |last1=Janssen |first1=Michel |last2=Renn |first2=Jürgen |date=2015 |title=Arch and scaffold: How Einstein found his field equations |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/68/11/30/414987/Arch-and-scaffold-How-Einstein-found-his-field |journal=Physics Today |volume=68 |issue=11 |pages=30–36 |doi=10.1063/PT.3.2979|bibcode=2015PhT....68k..30J |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-002A-8ED7-1 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He explains the [[perihelion]] of Mercury and calculates [[gravitational lens]]ing correctly and introduces the [[Post-Newtonian expansion|post-Newtonian approximation]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1915 |title=Erklärung der Perihelbewegung des Merkur aus der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie |trans-title=Explanation of the Perihelion Motion of Mercury from the General Theory of Relativity |journal=Preussische Akademie der Wissenschaften, Sitzungsberichte |pages=831–839|bibcode=1915SPAW.......831E }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1916 |title=Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie |trans-title=The Foundation of the General Theory of Relativity |url=https://www.physik.uni-augsburg.de/annalen/history/einstein-papers/1916_49_769-822.pdf |journal=Annalen der Physik |volume=4 |issue=7 |pages=769–822|doi=10.1002/andp.19163540702 |bibcode=1916AnP...354..769E }}</ref>
* 1915 – [[David Hilbert]] independently introduces the [[Einstein–Hilbert action|Einstein-Hilbert action]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Die Grundlagen der Physik |url= |journal=Nachrichten von der Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen – Mathematisch-Physikalische Klasse |volume=3 |issue= |pages=395–407 |year=1915 |trans-title=Foundations of Physics |language=German |doi= |jfm= |author-link=David Hilbert |author-first=David |author-last=Hilbert}}</ref><ref name=":13" /> Hilbert also recognizes the connection between the Einstein equations and the [[Gauss–Bonnet theorem|Gauss-Bonnet theorem]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Marsden |first1=Jerrold |title=Vector Calculus |last2=Tromba |first2=Anthony |publisher=W. H. Freeman Company |year=2012 |isbn=978-1-4292-1508-4 |edition=6th |location=New York |page=422 |chapter=7.7 Applications to Differential Geometry, Physics, and Forms of Life |author-link=Jerrold E. Marsden}}</ref>
* 1916 – [[Karl Schwarzschild]] publishes the [[Schwarzschild metric]] about a month after Einstein published his general theory of relativity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schwarzschild |first=Karl |date=1916 |title=Über das Gravitationsfeld eines Massenpunktes nach der Einstein'schen Theorie. |trans-title=On the Gravitational Field of a Point Mass According to Einstein's Theory |url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/de:%C3%9Cber_das_Gravitationsfeld_eines_Massenpunktes_nach_der_Einsteinschen_Theorie |journal=Sitzungsberichte der Königlich-Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schwarzschild |first=Karl |date=1916 |title=Über das Gravitationsfeld einer Kugel aus inkompressibler Flüssigkeit |trans-title=On the Gravitational Field of a Sphere of Incompressible Fluid |journal=Sitzungsberichte der Königlich-Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften}}</ref> This was the first solution to the Einstein field equations other than the trivial flat space solution.<ref name="Levy">{{cite journal |last1=Levy |first1=Adam |date=January 11, 2021 |title=How black holes morphed from theory to reality |url=https://knowablemagazine.org/article/physical-world/2021/how-black-holes-morphed-theory-reality |journal=Knowable Magazine |doi=10.1146/knowable-010921-1 |access-date=25 March 2022 |doi-access=free|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Eisenstaedt, 1989">Eisenstaedt, "The Early Interpretation of the Schwarzschild Solution," in D. Howard and [[John Stachel|J. Stachel]] (eds), Einstein and the History of General Relativity: Einstein Studies, Vol. 1, pp. 213-234. Boston: Birkhauser, 1989.</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Bartusiak |first=Marcia |title=Black Hole: How An Idea Abandoned by Newtonians, Hated by Einstein, and Gambled on by Hawking Became Loved |publisher=Yale University Press |year=2015 |isbn=978-0-300-21085-9 |location=New Haven, CT |chapter=Chapter 3: One Would Then Find Oneself... in a Geometrical Fairyland}}</ref>
* 1916 – [[Hans Reissner]] obtains the [[Reissner–Nordström metric|Reissner–Nordström solution]],<ref>{{cite journal |last=Reissner|first=H.|date=1916|title=Über die Eigengravitation des elektrischen Feldes nach der Einsteinschen Theorie|url=https://zenodo.org/record/1447315|journal=Annalen der Physik|language=en|volume=355|issue=9|pages=106–120|bibcode=1916AnP...355..106R|doi=10.1002/andp.19163550905|issn=0003-3804}}</ref> rediscovered in 1918 by [[Gunnar Nordström]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Nordström|first=G.|date=1918|title=On the Energy of the Gravitational Field in Einstein's Theory|journal=Koninklijke Nederlandsche Akademie van Wetenschappen Proceedings|volume=20|issue=2|pages=1238–1245|bibcode=1918KNAB...20.1238N}}</ref>
* 1916 – Albert Einstein predicts the existence of [[gravitational wave]]s, traveling at the speed of light.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1916 |title=Näherungsweise Integration der Feldgleichungen der Gravitation |trans-title=Approximate Integration of the Field Equations of Gravitation |journal=Preussische Akademie der Wissenschaften, Sitzungsberichte |language=German |pages=688–696|bibcode=1916SPAW.......688E }}</ref><ref name=":03" />{{Reference page|pages=279-80}}
* 1916 – [[Willem de Sitter]] predicts the [[geodetic effect]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=de Sitter |first=W |year=1916 |title=On Einstein's Theory of Gravitation and its Astronomical Consequences |journal=Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. |volume=77 |pages=155–184 |bibcode=1916MNRAS..77..155D |doi=10.1093/mnras/77.2.155 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1917 – Albert Einstein applies his field equations to the entire Universe.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1917 |title=Kosmologische Betrachtungen zur allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie |trans-title=Cosmological Considerations in the General Theory of Relativity |journal=Preussische Akademie der Wissenschaften, Sitzungsberichte |language=German |volume=1 |pages=142–152}}</ref> [[Physical cosmology]] is born.<ref name=":22" />
* 1916-20 – [[Arthur Eddington]] studies the internal constitution of the stars.<ref name="eddington">The Internal Constitution of the Stars A. S. Eddington The Scientific Monthly Vol. 11, No. 4 (Oct., 1920), pp. 297–303 {{JSTOR|6491}}</ref><ref name="eddington2">{{cite journal |last1=Eddington |first1=A. S. |year=1916 |title=On the radiative equilibrium of the stars |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |volume=77 |pages=16–35 |bibcode=1916MNRAS..77...16E |doi=10.1093/mnras/77.1.16 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1918 – Albert Einstein derives the [[quadrupole formula]] for gravitational radiation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1918 |title=Gravitationswellen |trans-title=Gravitational Waves |journal=Preussische Akademie der Wissenschaften, Sitzungsberichte |language=German |pages=154–167}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Holz |first1=Daniel |last2=Hughes |first2=Scott |last3=Bernard |first3=Schultz |date=December 2018 |title=Measuring cosmic distances with standard sirens |journal=Physics Today |volume=71 |issue=12 |page=34|doi=10.1063/PT.3.4090 |bibcode=2018PhT....71l..34H |s2cid=125545290 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1918 – [[Emmy Noether]] publishes [[Noether's theorem]] and resolves the issue of local [[Conservation of energy|energy conservation]] in general relativity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Noether |first=Emmy |date=1918 |title=Invariante variationsprobleme |trans-title=Invariant Variation Problems |journal=Nachr. Ges. Wiss. Gottingen |language=German |issue=Math.-Phys. Kl 235}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Byers |first=Nina |author-link=Nina Byers |date=1998 |title=E. Noether's discovery of the deep connection between symmetries and conservation laws |journal=Proceedings of a Symposium on the Heritage of Emmy Noether |publisher=[[Bar-Ilan University]] |arxiv=physics/9807044 |bibcode=1998physics...7044B }}</ref>
* 1918 – [[Felix Klein]] applies the [[calculus of variations]] to deduce the conservation laws of general relativity.<ref name=":03" />{{Reference page|page=274}}
* 1918 – [[Josef Lense]] and [[Hans Thirring]] find the [[Gravitoelectromagnetism|gravitomagnetic]] [[frame-dragging]] of [[gyroscope]]s in the equations of general relativity.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Thirring |first=H. |date=1918 |title=Über die Wirkung rotierender ferner Massen in der Einsteinschen Gravitationstheorie |journal=Physikalische Zeitschrift |volume=19 |page=33 |bibcode=1918PhyZ...19...33T}} [On the Effect of Rotating Distant Masses in Einstein's Theory of Gravitation]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Thirring |first=H. |date=1921 |title=Berichtigung zu meiner Arbeit: 'Über die Wirkung rotierender Massen in der Einsteinschen Gravitationstheorie' |journal=Physikalische Zeitschrift |volume=22 |page=29 |bibcode=1921PhyZ...22...29T}} [Correction to my paper "On the Effect of Rotating Distant Masses in Einstein's Theory of Gravitation"]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Lense |first=J. |author2=Thirring, H. |date=1918 |title=Über den Einfluss der Eigenrotation der Zentralkörper auf die Bewegung der Planeten und Monde nach der Einsteinschen Gravitationstheorie |journal=Physikalische Zeitschrift |volume=19 |pages=156–163 |bibcode=1918PhyZ...19..156L}} [On the Influence of the Proper Rotation of Central Bodies on the Motions of Planets and Moons According to Einstein's Theory of Gravitation]</ref>
* 1919 – Arthur Eddington leads a [[Eddington experiment|solar eclipse expedition]] which detects gravitational deflection of light by the Sun,<ref name="Eddington1920">{{cite journal |last=Dyson |first=F.W. |author2=Eddington, A.S. |author3=Davidson, C.R. |date=1920 |title=A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun's Gravitational Field, from Observations Made at the Solar eclipse of May 29, 1919 |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1432106 |journal=[[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences|Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A]] |volume=220 |issue=571–581 |pages=291–333 |bibcode=1920RSPTA.220..291D |doi=10.1098/rsta.1920.0009 |doi-access=free}}</ref> which, despite opinion to the contrary, survives modern scrutiny.<ref name="PhysToday">{{Cite journal |last=Kennefick |first=Daniel |date=1 March 2009 |title=Testing relativity from the 1919 eclipse – a question of bias |journal=Physics Today |volume=62 |issue=3 |pages=37–42 |bibcode=2009PhT....62c..37K |doi=10.1063/1.3099578 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Other teams fail for reasons of [[World War I|war]] and politics.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kaiser |first=David |date=November 6, 2015 |title=Opinion {{!}} How Politics Shaped General Relativity |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/11/08/opinion/how-politics-shaped-general-relativity.html |access-date=August 26, 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

=== 1920s ===
[[File:CMB Timeline300 no WMAP.jpg|thumb|right|The history and [[expansion of the universe]]]]
* 1921 – [[Theodor Kaluza]] demonstrates that a [[Kaluza–Klein theory|five-dimensional version of Einstein's equations]] unifies [[gravitation]] and [[electromagnetism]].<ref name="kal">{{cite journal |last=Kaluza |first=Theodor |date=1921 |title=Zum Unitätsproblem in der Physik |journal=Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin. (Math. Phys.) |pages=966–972 |bibcode=1921SPAW.......966K |language=de}}</ref> This idea is later extended by [[Oskar Klein]] to incorporate quantum mechanics.<ref name=KN>{{cite journal |last=Klein |first=Oskar |date=1926 |journal=Nature |volume=118 |issue=2971 |page=516 |doi=10.1038/118516a0 |title=The Atomicity of Electricity as a Quantum Theory Law |bibcode= 1926Natur.118..516K |s2cid=4127863 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":23">{{Cite journal |last1=Freedman |first1=Daniel Z. |author-link1=Daniel Z. Freedman |last2=van Niewenhuizen |first2=Peter |author-link2=Peter van Nieuwenhuizen |date=March 1985 |title=The Hidden Dimensions of Spacetime |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/the-hidden-dimensions-of-spacetime/ |journal=Scientific American |volume=252 |issue=3 |pages=74–81 |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0385-74|bibcode=1985SciAm.252c..74F |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Pais |first=Abraham |title=The Genius of Science: A Portrait Gallery of Twentieth-Century Physicists |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2000 |isbn=0-19-850614-7 |location=New York |chapter=Chapter 7: Oskar Klein}}</ref>
* 1922 – [[Alexander Friedmann]] derives the [[Friedmann equations]].<ref name="af1922">{{cite journal |last=Friedman |first=Alexander |author-link=Alexander Friedmann |date=December 1922 |title=Über die Krümmung des Raumes |journal=[[Zeitschrift für Physik]] |language=de |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=377–386 |bibcode=1922ZPhy...10..377F |doi=10.1007/BF01332580 |s2cid=125190902}} Translated in: {{cite journal |last=Friedmann |first=Alexander |author-link=Alexander Friedmann |date=December 1999 |title=On the Curvature of Space |journal=[[General Relativity and Gravitation]] |volume=31 |issue=12 |pages=1991–2000 |bibcode=1999GReGr..31.1991F |doi=10.1023/A:1026751225741 |s2cid=122950995}}</ref><ref name=":22" />
* 1922 – [[Enrico Fermi]] introduces the [[Fermi coordinates]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Marzlin |first1=Karl-Peter |year=1994 |title=The physical meaning of Fermi coordinates |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |volume=26 |issue=6 |pages=619–636 |arxiv=gr-qc/9402010 |bibcode=1994GReGr..26..619M |doi=10.1007/BF02108003 |s2cid=17918026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Segrè |first1=Gino |title=The Pope of Physics |last2=Hoerlin |first2=Bettina |publisher=Henry Holt and Co. |year=2016 |isbn=978-1-627-79005-5 |page=27 |chapter=Chapter 4: Student Days}}</ref> This is developed further in 1932 by Arthur Walker into the [[Fermi–Walker transport|Fermi-Walker transport]].<ref name=":02" />
* 1923 – [[George David Birkhoff]] proves [[Birkhoff's theorem (relativity)|Birkhoff's theorem]] on the uniqueness of the Schwarzschild solution.<ref name=":92">{{Cite book |last=Thorne |first=Kip |author-link=Kip Thorne |title=Black Holes and Time Warps: Einstein's Outrageous Legacy |title-link=Black Holes and Time Warps |publisher=W. W. Norton & Company |year=1994 |isbn=0-393-03505-0 |location=New York}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=213}}
* 1924 – Arthur Eddington calculates the [[Eddington luminosity|Eddington limit]].<ref name="eddington3">{{cite journal |last1=Eddington |first1=A. S. |date=1924 |title=On the relation between the masses and luminosities of the stars |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |volume=84 |issue=5 |pages=308–333 |bibcode=1924MNRAS..84..308E |doi=10.1093/mnras/84.5.308 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1924 – [[Cornelius Lanczos]] discovers the [[van Stockum dust]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lanczos |first=Cornelius |date=1924 |title=Über eine stationäre Kosmologie im Sinne der Einsteinschen Gravitationstheorie |trans-title=On a static cosmology in the sense of Einstein's theory of gravity |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01328251 |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik |language=German |volume=21 |issue=1 |pages=73–110|doi=10.1007/BF01328251 |bibcode=1924ZPhy...21...73L |url-access=subscription }}</ref> later rediscovered by [[Willem Jacob van Stockum]] in 1938.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=van Stuckum |first=Willem Jacob |date=1938 |title=The gravitational field of a distribution of particles rotating around an axis of symmetry |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh |volume=57 |pages=135–154 |doi=10.1017/S0370164600013699}}</ref>
* 1925 – [[Walter Sydney Adams|Walter Adams]] measures the gravitational redshift of the light emitted by the companion of Sirius B, a [[white dwarf]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Adams |first1=W. S. |date=1925 |title=The Relativity Displacement of the Spectral Lines in the Companion of Sirius |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=11 |issue=7 |pages=382–387 |bibcode=1925PNAS...11..382A |doi=10.1073/pnas.11.7.382 |pmc=1086032 |pmid=16587023 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1927 – [[Georges Lemaître]] publishes his hypothesis of the [[Big Bang|primeval atom]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Big bang theory is introduced – 1927 |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/aso/databank/entries/dp27bi.html |access-date=31 July 2014 |website=A Science Odyssey |publisher=WGBH}}</ref><ref name=":22" />
* 1929 – [[Edwin Hubble]] published the [[Hubble's Law|law later named for him]].<ref name="hubble">{{cite journal |last=Hubble |first=Edwin |author-link=Edwin Hubble |date=15 March 1929 |title=A Relation Between Distance and Radial Velocity Among Extra-Galactic Nebulae |url=https://apod.nasa.gov/debate/1996/hub_1929.html |url-status=live |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]] |volume=15 |issue=3 |pages=168–173 |bibcode=1929PNAS...15..168H |doi=10.1073/pnas.15.3.168 |pmc=522427 |pmid=16577160 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061001060258/https://apod.nasa.gov/debate/1996/hub_1929.html |archive-date=1 October 2006 |access-date=28 November 2019 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== 1930s ===
* [[File:Einstein_blackboard.jpg|thumb|Einstein lectured on cosmology at the University of Oxford in 1931 using this [[Einstein's Blackboard|blackboard]], now preserved at the Oxford's [[History of Science Museum, Oxford|Museum of the History of Science]]. The last expression is Einstein's estimate for the age of the Universe.]]1931 – [[Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar]] studies the [[Chandrasekhar limit|stability]] of [[white dwarf]]s.<ref name="chandra3">{{cite journal |last1=Chandrasekhar |first1=S. |year=1931 |title=The Density of White Dwarf Stars |journal=Philosophical Magazine |volume=11 |issue=70 |pages=592–596 |doi=10.1080/14786443109461710 |s2cid=119906976}}</ref><ref name="chandra4">{{cite journal |last1=Chandrasekhar |first1=S. |year=1931 |title=The Maximum Mass of Ideal White Dwarfs |journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=74 |pages=81–82 |bibcode=1931ApJ....74...81C |doi=10.1086/143324|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1931 – Georges Lemaître and Arthur Eddington predict the [[Expansion of the universe|expansion of the Universe]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=September 1966 |title=Obituary: Georges Lemaitre |journal=Physics Today |volume=19 |issue=9 |pages=119–121 |doi=10.1063/1.3048455 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lemaître |first1=Georges |last2=Eddington |first2=Stanley |date=March 1931 |title=The Expanding Universe |url=https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/91/5/490/985169 |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |volume=91 |issue=5 |pages=490–501 |doi=10.1093/mnras/91.5.490|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1931 – Albert Einstein introduces his [[cosmological constant]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |date=1931 |title=Zum kosmologischen Problem der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie |trans-title=On the Cosmological Problem of the General Theory of Relativity |journal=Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Physikalisch-mathematische Klasse |language=German |pages=235–237}}</ref>
* 1932 – Albert Einstein and Willem de Sitter propose the [[Einstein–de Sitter universe|Einstein-de Sitter cosmological model]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Einstein |author2=and De Sitter |date=1932 |title=On the relation between the expansion and the mean density of the universe |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=18 |issue=3 |pages=213–214 |bibcode=1932PNAS...18..213E |doi=10.1073/pnas.18.3.213 |pmc=1076193 |pmid=16587663 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1932 – [[John Cockcroft]] and [[Ernest Walton]] verify Einstein's mass-energy equation by an experiment artificially [[Nuclear transmutation|transmuting]] lithium into helium.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cockcroft |first1=John |last2=Walton |first2=Ernest |date=April 1932 |title=Disintegration of Lithium by Swift Protons |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/129649a0 |journal=Nature |volume=129 |issue=649 |page=649 |doi=10.1038/129649a0|bibcode=1932Natur.129..649C }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Poffenberger |first1=Leah |last2=Levine |first2=Alaina G. |date=April 2019 |editor-last=Voss |editor-first=David |title=April 14, 1932: Cockcroft and Walton Split the Atom |url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201904/history.cfm |department=This Month in History |journal=APS News |publisher=American Physical Society (APS) |volume=28 |issue=4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190501014634/https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201904/history.cfm|archive-date=May 1, 2019}}</ref>
* 1933 – [[Karl Guthe Jansky|Karl Jansky]] discovers astronomical radio sources.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=538}}
* 1934 – [[Dmitry Blokhintsev]] and F. M. Gal'perin coin the term '[[graviton]]'.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=D. I. |first1=Blokhintsev |last2=F. M. |first2=Gal'perin |date=1934 |title=Гипотеза нейтрино и закон сохранения энергии |trans-title=Neutrino hypothesis and conservation of energy |journal=Pod Znamenem Marxisma |language=Russian |volume=6 |pages=147–157 |isbn=978-5-04-008956-7}}</ref> [[Paul Dirac]] reintroduces it in 1959.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Farmelo |first=Graham |author-link=Graham Farmelo |title=The Strangest Man: The Hidden Life of Paul Dirac, Quantum Genius |publisher=Faber and Faber |year=2009 |isbn=978-0-571-22278-0 |pages=367–368 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Debnath">{{Cite journal |last=Debnath |first=Lokenath |author-link=Lokenath Debnath |date=2013 |title=A short biography of Paul A. M. Dirac and historical development of Dirac delta function |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0020739X.2013.770091 |journal=International Journal of Mathematical Education in Science and Technology |language=en |volume=44 |issue=8 |pages=1201–1223 |doi=10.1080/0020739X.2013.770091 |bibcode=2013IJMES..44.1201D |issn=0020-739X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1934 – [[Walter Baade]] and [[Fritz Zwicky]] predict the existence of [[neutron star]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Baade |first1=Walter |last2=Zwicky |first2=Fritz |date=1934 |title=Remarks on Super-novae and Cosmic Rays |url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/5999/1/BAApr34.pdf |journal=Physical Review |volume=46 |issue=1 |pages=76–77 |doi=10.1103/PHYSREV.46.76.2|bibcode=1934PhRv...46...76B }}</ref> Although their details are wrong, their basic idea is now accepted.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McCormick |first=Katie |date=July 18, 2023 |title=Ultracold Gases Can Probe Neutron Star Guts |work=Scientific American |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/ultracold-gases-can-probe-neutron-star-guts/ |access-date=July 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230731121927/https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/ultracold-gases-can-probe-neutron-star-guts/ |archive-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref>
* 1935 – Albert Einstein and [[Nathan Rosen]] derive the [[Wormhole|Einstein-Rosen bridge]], the first wormhole solution.<ref name="ER">A. Einstein and N. Rosen, "The Particle Problem in the General Theory of Relativity," ''Phys. Rev.'' '''48'''(73) (1935).</ref>
* 1935 – [[Howard P. Robertson|Howard Robertson]] and [[Arthur Geoffrey Walker|Arthur Walker]] obtain the [[Robertson-Walker metric]].<ref name=":02">{{Cite journal |last1=Hitchin |first1=N. J. |author-link=Nigel Hitchin |year=2006 |title=Arthur Geoffrey Walker. 17 July 1909 -- 31 March 2001: Elected FRS 1955 |journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] |volume=52 |pages=413–421 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2006.0028  |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1936 – Albert Einstein predicts that a gravitational lens brightens the light coming from a distant object to the observer.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Einstein |first=Albert |title=Lens-Like Action of a Star by the Deviation of Light in the Gravitational Field |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.84.2188.506 |journal=Science |year=1936 |volume=84 |issue=2188 |pages=506–507 |doi=10.1126/science.84.2188.506|pmid=17769014 |bibcode=1936Sci....84..506E |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* [[File:Einstein cross (cropped).jpg|thumb|The [[Einstein Cross]] is an example of gravitational lensing at work. This one was discovered in 1985.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Huchra, J. |display-authors=et al |year=1985 |title=2237 + 0305: A new and unusual gravitational lens |journal=[[Astronomical Journal]] |volume=90 |pages=691–696 |bibcode=1985AJ.....90..691H |doi=10.1086/113777 |doi-access=free}}</ref>]]1937 – Fritz Zwicky states that [[galaxy|galaxies]] could act as [[gravitational lens]]es.<ref>{{cite journal |author=F.
