Zwicky |year=1937 |title=Nebulae as Gravitational lenses |url=http://authors.library.caltech.edu/5611/1/ZWIpr37a.pdf |url-status=live |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=51 |issue=4 |page=290 |bibcode=1937PhRv...51..290Z |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.51.290 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131226004748/http://authors.library.caltech.edu/5611/1/ZWIpr37a.pdf |archive-date=2013-12-26}}</ref>
* 1937 – Albert Einstein and Nathan Rosen obtain the [[Einstein-Rosen metric]], the first exact solution describing gravitational waves.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Einstein, Albert |author2=Rosen, Nathan |name-list-style=amp |date=1937 |title=On Gravitational waves |journal=Journal of the Franklin Institute |volume=223 |pages=43–54 |bibcode=1937FrInJ.223...43E |doi=10.1016/S0016-0032(37)90583-0}}</ref>
* 1938 – Albert Einstein, Leopold Infeld, and Banesh Hoffmann obtain the [[Einstein–Infeld–Hoffmann equations|Einstein-Infeld-Hoffmann equations]] of motion.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Einstein |first1=Albert |last2=Infeld |first2=Leopold |last3=Hoffmann |first3=Banesh |date=1938 |title=The Gravitational Equations and the Problem of Motion |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=39 |issue=1 |pages=65–100 |doi=10.2307/1968714|jstor=1968714 }}</ref>
* 1939 – [[Hans Bethe]] shows that nuclear fusion is responsible for energy production inside stars,<ref name="frs">{{cite journal |last1=Lee |first1=S. |last2=Brown |first2=G. E. |date=2007 |title=Hans Albrecht Bethe. 2 July 1906 — 6 March 2005: Elected ForMemRS 1957 |journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] |volume=53 |page=1 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2007.0018 |doi-access=free}}</ref> building upon the [[Kelvin–Helmholtz mechanism]]. [[Charles Critchfield]] independently reaches the same conclusion.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=191}}
* 1939 – [[Richard C. Tolman|Richard Tolman]] solves the Einstein field equations in the case of [[Static spherically symmetric perfect fluid|a spherical fluid drop]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tolman |first=Richard C. |date=1939 |title=Static Solutions of Einstein's Field Equations for Spheres of Fluid |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.55.364 |journal=Physical Review |volume=55 |issue=364 |pages=364–373 |bibcode=1939PhRv...55..364T |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.55.364|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":6" />{{Reference page|pages=31-2}}
* 1938-9 – [[Robert Serber]], [[George Volkoff]], Richard Tolman, and J. Robert Oppenheimer determine the [[Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff limit]] for the stability of neutron stars.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Oppenheimer |first1=J.R. |last2=Serber |first2=Robert |author-link2=Robert Serber |year=1938 |title=On the Stability of Stellar Neutron Cores |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=54 |issue=7 |page=540 |bibcode=1938PhRv...54..540O |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.54.540}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Oppenheimer |first1=J.R. |last2=Volkoff |first2=G.M. |author-link2=George Volkoff |year=1939 |title=On Massive Neutron Cores |url=http://www.mpia-hd.mpg.de/home/fendt/Lehre/Vorlesung_CO/1939_oppenheimer_volkoff.pdf |url-status=live |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=55 |issue=4 |pages=374–381 |bibcode=1939PhRv...55..374O |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.55.374 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116084323/http://www.mpia-hd.mpg.de/home/fendt/Lehre/Vorlesung_CO/1939_oppenheimer_volkoff.pdf |archive-date=January 16, 2014 |access-date=January 15, 2014}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite book |last1=Pais |first1=Abraham |author-link=Abraham Pais |title=J. Robert Oppenheimer: A Life |last2=Crease |first2=Robert |author-link2=Robert P. Crease |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2006 |isbn=978-0-195-32712-0 |pages=}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=31-2}}
* 1939 – [[J. Robert Oppenheimer]] and [[Hartland Snyder]] publish the [[Oppenheimer–Snyder model|Oppenheimer-Snyder model]] for the continued gravitational contraction of a star.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Oppenheimer |first1=J.R. |last2=Snyder |first2=H. |author-link2=Hartland Snyder |year=1939 |title=On Continued Gravitational Contraction |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=56 |issue=5 |pages=455–459 |bibcode=1939PhRv...56..455O |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.56.455 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":6" />{{Reference page|pages=31-2}}<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bartels |first=Megan |date=July 21, 2023 |title=Oppenheimer Almost Discovered Black Holes Before He Became 'Destroyer of Worlds' |work=Scientific American |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/oppenheimer-almost-discovered-black-holes-before-he-became-destroyer-of-worlds/ |access-date=July 26, 2023}}</ref>

=== 1940s ===
[[File:Big Bang and Steady-State Theory 2.png|thumb|Comparing the Big Bang and Steady State models of the Universe]]
* 1946 – First [[radio telescope]]s and [[Radio interferometer|interferometers]] built in the United Kingdom and Australia.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=539}}
* 1948 – [[Ralph Alpher]], [[Hans Bethe]], and [[George Gamow]] explain the [[Nucleosynthesis|origin of the chemical elements]] using the notion of an expanding universe.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Alpher|first1=Ralph A.|last2=Bethe|first2=Hans|last3=Gamow|first3=George|date=April 1, 1948|title=The Origin of Chemical Elements|journal=[[Physical Review]]|volume=73|issue=7|pages=803–804|bibcode=1948PhRv...73..803A|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.73.803|pmid=|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1948 – Ralph Alpher and [[Robert Herman]] predict the [[cosmic microwave background]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Alpher |first1=R. A. |last2=Herman |first2=R. C. |date=1948 |title=On the Relative Abundance of the Elements |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=74 |issue=12 |pages=1737–1742 |bibcode=1948PhRv...74.1737A |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.74.1737}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Alpher |first1=R. A. |last2=Herman |first2=R. C. |date=1948 |title=Evolution of the Universe |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=162 |issue=4124 |pages=774–775 |bibcode=1948Natur.162..774A |doi=10.1038/162774b0 |s2cid=4113488}}</ref>
* 1949 – [[Fred Hoyle]] coins the term "[[Big Bang]]" theory in contrast with his "Steady State" model, though the term ''Big Bang'' only becomes widespread in the 1970s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kragh |first=Helge |author-link=Helge Kragh |date=April 2013 |title=Big Bang: the etymology of a name |url=https://academic.oup.com/astrogeo/article/54/2/2.28/302975 |journal=Astronomy & Geophysics |volume=54 |issue=2 |pages=2.28–2.30 |doi=10.1093/astrogeo/att035}}</ref>
* 1949 – [[Cornelius Lanczos]] introduces the [[Lanczos tensor|Lanczos potential]] for the [[Weyl tensor]].<ref name="Lanczos1949">{{cite journal |last=Lanczos |first=Cornelius |date=July 1, 1949 |title=Lagrangian Multiplier and Riemannian Spaces |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |publisher=American Physical Society (APS) |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=497–502 |bibcode=1949RvMP...21..497L |doi=10.1103/revmodphys.21.497 |issn=0034-6861 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1949 – [[Kurt Gödel]] discovers [[Gödel metric|Gödel's solution]] and introduces [[Lie group]]s to cosmology.<ref>Gödel, K., [http://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.21.447 "An Example of a New Type of Cosmological Solutions of Einstein's Field Equations of Gravitation"], ''[[Rev. Mod. Phys.]]'' '''21''', 447, published July 1, 1949.</ref> [[Abraham H. Taub|Abraham Taub]] independently applies the same mathematical method in 1951.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Taub |first=Abraham |date=1951 |title=Empty Space-Times Admitting a Three Parameter Group of Motions |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/B:GERG.0000048984.29896.12 |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |volume=36 |issue=12 |pages=2699–2719 |doi=10.1023/B:GERG.0000048984.29896.12|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":19">{{Cite journal |last=Trautman |first=Andrzej |date=January 1986 |title=Review: Theodore Frankel, ''Gravitational Curvature: An Introduction to Einstein's Theory'', and Hans Stephani, ''General Relativity: An Introduction to the Theory of the Gravitational Field'', and Robert M. Wald, ''General Relativity'' |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society-new-series/volume-14/issue-1/Review--Theodore-Frankel-Gravitational-curvature-an-introduction-to-Einsteins/bams/1183552796.full |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=152–158 |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1986-15425-X |doi-access=free }}</ref>

===1950s===
* 1950 – [[John Lighton Synge]] presents the first maximal analytic extension of the Schwarzschild metric.<ref>Synge, John Lighton. "The gravitational field of a particle." Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy. Section A: Mathematical and Physical Sciences. Vol. 53. Royal Irish Academy, 1950.</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Florides |first=Petros S. |author-link=Petros Serghiou Florides |date=December 12, 2008 |title=John Lighton Synge. 23 March 1897 — 30 March 1995 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=2008 |issue=54 |pages=401–24 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2007.0040 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1952 – [[Yvonne Choquet-Bruhat]] proves that the [[Initial value problem|initial-value problem]] of the Einstein field equations in vacuum is [[Well-posed problem|well-posed]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fourès-Bruhat |first=Yvonne |date=1952 |title=Théorème d'existence pour certains systèmes d'équations aux dérivées partielles non linéaires |trans-title=Existence Theorem for Certain Systems of Non-Linear Partial Differential Equations |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/acta-mathematica/volume-88/issue-none/Th%c3%a9or%c3%a8me-dexistence-pour-certains-syst%c3%a8mes-d%c3%a9quations-aux-d%c3%a9riv%c3%a9es-partielles-non/10.1007/BF02392131.full |journal=Acta Mathematica |language=French |volume=88 |pages=141–225 |doi=10.1007/BF02392131 |bibcode=1952AcMa...88..141F }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Will |first=Clifford |author-link=Clifford Martin Will |date=2015 |title=Focus issue: Milestones of general relativity |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/0264-9381/page/Focus%20issue%20on%20Milestones%20of%20general%20relativity |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=32 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/32/12/120201 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ringström |first=Hans |date=2015 |title=Origins and development of the Cauchy problem in general relativity |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/32/12/124003/pdf |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=32 |issue=12 |article-number=124003 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/32/12/124003|bibcode=2015CQGra..32l4003R |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1954 – [[Suraj N. Gupta|Suraj Gupta]] sketches how to derive the equations of general relativity from quantum field theory for a massless spin-2 particle (the [[graviton]]).<ref name="PPS">{{cite journal |last=Gupta |first=Suraj N. |year=1952 |title=Quantization of Einstein's Gravitational Field: General Treatment |journal=[[Proceedings of the Physical Society]] |series=Series A |volume=65 |issue=8 |pages=608–619 |bibcode=1952PPSA...65..608G |doi=10.1088/0370-1298/65/8/304}}</ref> His procedure is later carried out by [[Stanley Deser]] in 1970.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Deser |first=Stanley |date=1970 |title=Self-interaction and gauge invariance |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00759198 |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=9–18 |doi=10.1007/BF00759198|arxiv=gr-qc/0411023 |bibcode=1970GReGr...1....9D |s2cid=14295121 }}</ref><ref name=":20">{{Cite book |last1=Feynman |first1=Richard |title=Feynman Lectures on Gravitations |last2=Morinigo |first2=Fernando B. |last3=Wagner |first3=William G. |publisher=Westview |year=2003 |isbn=978-0-813-34038-8 |editor-last=Hatfield |editor-first=Brian |location=Boulder, Colorado |chapter=Foreword by John Preskill and Kip Thorne |chapter-url=http://www.theory.caltech.edu/~preskill/pubs/preskill-1995-feynman.pdf}}</ref>
* 1955 – [[John Archibald Wheeler]] proposes the existence of [[Quantum foam|gravitational quantum fluctuations]] and discusses the importance of the [[Planck units|Planck length]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Geons|bibcode=1955PhRv...97..511W|last=Wheeler|first=John A.|journal=[[Physical Review]]|date=January 1955|volume=97|issue=2|pages=511–536|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.97.511}}</ref><ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=540}}
* 1955-56 – [[Robert Kraichnan]] shows that under the appropriate assumptions, Einstein's field equations of gravitation arise from the [[quantum field theory]] of a massless spin-2 particle coupled to the stress-energy tensor.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Kraichnan |year=1955 |title=Special-Relativistic Derivation of Generally Covariant Gravitation Theory |journal=Physical Review |volume=98 |issue=4 |pages=1118–1122 |bibcode=1955PhRv...98.1118K |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.98.1118}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Kraichnan |year=1956 |title=Possibility of unequal gravitational and inertial masses |journal=Physical Review |volume=101 |issue=1 |pages=482–488 |bibcode=1956PhRv..101..482K |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.101.482}}</ref> This follows from his unpublished work as an undergraduate in 1947.<ref name=":20" />
* [[File:PM vs PN expansion EN.svg|thumb|Some methods of approximation in general relativity]]1956 – [[Bruno Bertotti|Bruno Berlotti]] develops the [[post-Minkowskian expansion]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bertotti |first=B. |date=1956-10-01 |title=On gravitational motion |journal=Il Nuovo Cimento |language=en |volume=4 |issue=4 |pages=898–906 |bibcode=1956NCim....4..898B |doi=10.1007/BF02746175 |issn=1827-6121 |s2cid=120443098}}</ref>
* 1957 – [[Felix A. E. Pirani]] uses [[Petrov classification]] to understand [[gravitational radiation]].
* 1957 – [[Richard Feynman]] introduces his [[sticky bead argument]].<ref name="Feynman">{{cite book |last1=Dewitt |first1=Cécile M. |last2=Rickles |first2=Dean |year=1957 |title=An Expanded Version of the Remarks by R.P. Feynman on the Reality of Gravitational Waves |url=http://www.edition-open-access.de/sources/5/34/index.html |series=EOS – Sources |publisher=Wright-Patterson Air Force Base |isbn=978-3-945561-29-4 |access-date=27 September 2016}}</ref><ref name=":20" /> He later derives the quadrupole formula in a letter to [[Victor Weisskopf]] (1961).<ref name=":20" />
* 1957 – [[Chapel Hill Conference]] on the Role of Gravitation in Physics held in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]].<ref name=":03" />{{Reference page|page=270}}
* 1957-8 – [[John Archibald Wheeler|John Wheeler]] discusses the breakdown of classical general relativity near [[gravitational singularity|singularities]] and the need for [[quantum gravity]].<ref name=":22" />
* 1958 – [[David Finkelstein]] presents [[Eddington–Finkelstein coordinates|a coordinate transformation]] that removes the Schwarzschild radius as a singularity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Finkelstein |first=David |date=1958 |title=Past-Future Asymmetry of the Gravitational Field of a Point Particle |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.110.965 |journal=Physical Review |volume=110 |issue=4 |pages=965–967 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.110.965|bibcode=1958PhRv..110..965F |url-access=subscription }}</ref> It is previously introduced by Arthur Eddington.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|pages=244-5}}
* 1959 – [[Robert Pound]] and [[Glen Rebka]] propose the [[Pound–Rebka experiment]], first precision test of [[gravitational redshift]]. The experiment relies on the [[Mössbauer effect]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pound |first1=Robert |last2=Rebka |first2=Glen |date=1959 |title=Gravitational Red-Shift in Nuclear Resonance |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=3 |issue=439 |pages=439–441 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.3.439|bibcode=1959PhRvL...3..439P |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1959 – [[Hermann Bondi|Herman Bondi]], Felix Pirani, and [[Ivor Robinson (physicist)|Ivor Robinson]] discuss exact [[gravitational plane wave]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bondi |first1=Hermann |last2=Pirani |first2=Felix |last3=Robinson |first3=Ivor |date=1959 |title=Gravitational waves in general relativity III. Exact plane waves |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rspa/article-abstract/251/1267/519/10553/Gravitational-waves-in-general-relativity-III?redirectedFrom=fulltext |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A |volume=251 |issue=1267 |pages=519–533 |doi=10.1098/rspa.1959.0124|bibcode=1959RSPSA.251..519B |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1959 – Lluís Bel introduces [[Bel–Robinson tensor]] and the [[Bel decomposition]] of the [[Riemann tensor]].
* 1959 – [[Arthur Komar]] introduces the [[Komar mass]].
* 1959 – [[Richard Arnowitt]], Stanley Deser and [[Charles W. Misner]] developed [[ADM formalism]].
* 1959 – [[Roger Penrose]] and [[Nelson James Terrell|James Terrell]] independently predict the [[The Terrell-Penrose Effect|Terrell–Penrose effect]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Penrose |first=Roger |date=January 1959 |title=The apparent shape of a relativistically moving sphere |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-proceedings-of-the-cambridge-philosophical-society/article/abs/apparent-shape-of-a-relativistically-moving-sphere/DD30A7EBF858269BB2B258C29037AC67 |journal=Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society |volume=55 |issue=1 |pages=137–9 |doi=10.1017/S0305004100033776|bibcode=1959PCPS...55..137P |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Terrell |first=James |date=November 1959 |title=Invisibility of the Lorentz Contraction |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.116.1041 |journal=Physical Review |volume=116 |issue=4 |pages=1041–45 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.116.1041 |bibcode=1959PhRv..116.1041T }}</ref>

===1960s===
* 1960 – [[Joseph Weber]] begins work on [[Weber bar|his bars]] for detecting [[gravitational wave]]s.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=541}}
* 1960 – [[Martin Kruskal]] and [[George Szekeres]] independently introduce the [[Kruskal–Szekeres coordinates]] for the [[Schwarzschild vacuum]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kruskal |first=Martin |date=1960 |title=Maximal Extension of Schwarzschild Metric |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.119.1743 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=119 |issue=1743 |pages=1743–1745 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.119.1743|bibcode=1960PhRv..119.1743K |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="rsbm">{{cite journal |last1=Gibbon |first1=John D. |last2=Cowley |first2=Steven C. |last3=Joshi |first3=Nalini |last4=MacCallum |first4=Malcolm A. H. |year=2017 |title=Martin David Kruskal. 28 September 1925 — 26 December 2006 |journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] |volume=64 |pages=261–284 |arxiv=1707.00139 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2017.0022  |doi-access=free|issn=0080-4606 |author-link2=Steven Cowley |author-link3=Nalini Joshi |s2cid=67365148}}</ref>
* 1960 – John Graves and Dieter Brill show that the Reissner–Nordström solution describe a spherical electrically charged black hole.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Graves |first1=John C. |last2=Brill |first2=Dieter R. |date=1960 |title=Oscillatory Character of Reissner-Nordström Metric for an Ideal Charged Wormhole |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.120.1507 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=120 |issue=4 |pages=1507–1513 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.120.1507|bibcode=1960PhRv..120.1507G |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=541}}
* 1960 – Ivor M. Robinson and [[Andrzej Trautman]] discover the Robinson-Trautman [[null dust solution]].<ref name="RobTrautmanPhysRevL1960_fixthis">{{cite journal|url=http://cdsads.u-strasbg.fr/abs/1960PhRvL...4..431R |title=Spherical Gravitational Waves |publisher=Cdsads.u-strasbg.fr |bibcode=1960PhRvL...4..431R |access-date=2012-07-20|last1=Robinson |first1=Ivor |last2=Trautman |first2=A. |journal=Physical Review Letters |year=1960 |volume=4 |issue=8 |page=431 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.431 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1960 – Robert Pound and Glen Rebka test the gravitational redshift predicted by the equivalence principle to approximately 1%.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pound |first1=Robert |last2=Rebka |first2=Glen |date=1960 |title=Apparent Weight of Photons |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=4 |issue=337 |pages=337–341 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337|bibcode=1960PhRvL...4..337P |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1961 –[[Tullio Regge]] introduces the [[Regge calculus]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Tullio E. Regge |author-link=Tullio E. Regge |year=1961 |title=General relativity without coordinates |journal=Nuovo Cimento |volume=19 |issue=3 |pages=558–571 |bibcode=1961NCim...19..558R |doi=10.1007/BF02733251 |s2cid=120696638}} Available (subscribers only) at [[doi:10.1007/BF02733251|Il Nuovo Cimento]]</ref>
* 1961 – [[Carl H. Brans]] and [[Robert H. Dicke]] introduce [[Brans–Dicke theory]], the first viable alternative theory with a clear physical motivation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bran |first1=Carl |last2=Dicke |first2=Robert |date=1961 |title=Mach's Principle and a Relativistic Theory of Gravitation |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.124.925 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=124 |issue=925 |pages=925–935 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.124.925|bibcode=1961PhRv..124..925B |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1961 – [[Pascual Jordan]] and [[Jürgen Ehlers]] develop the ''kinematic decomposition'' of a [[timelike congruence]],
* 1961 – Robert Dicke, Peter Roll, and R. Krotkov refine the [[Eötvös experiment]] to an accuracy of 10<sup>−11</sup>.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Roll |first1=P.G |last2=Krotkov |first2=R |last3=Dicke |first3=R.H |year=1964 |title=The equivalence of inertial and passive gravitational mass |journal=Annals of Physics |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=26 |issue=3 |pages=442–517 |bibcode=1964AnPhy..26..442R |doi=10.1016/0003-4916(64)90259-3 |issn=0003-4916}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dicke |first1=Robert H. |date=December 1961 |title=The Eötvös Experiment |journal=Scientific American |volume=205 |issue=6 |pages=84–95 |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican1261-84|bibcode=1961SciAm.205f..84D }}</ref>
* 1962 – John Wheeler and Robert Fuller show that the Einstein-Rosen bridge is unstable.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wheeler |first1=John |last2=Fuller |first2=Robert |date=1962 |title=Causality and Multiply Connected Space-Time |url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.128.919 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=128 |issue=919 |pages=919–929 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.128.919|bibcode=1962PhRv..128..919F |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1962 – Roger Penrose and [[Ezra T. Newman]] introduce the [[Newman–Penrose formalism]].
* 1962 – Ehlers and [[Wolfgang Kundt]] classify the symmetries of [[Pp-wave spacetimes]].
* 1962 –[[Joshua N. Goldberg|Joshua Goldberg]] and [[Rainer K. Sachs]] prove the [[Goldberg–Sachs theorem]].<ref name="original_paper">{{cite journal |last1=Goldberg |first1=J. N. |last2=Sachs |first2=R. K. |date=1962 |title=A theorem on Petrov types (republished January 2009) |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |volume=41 |issue=2 |pages=433–444 |doi=10.1007/s10714-008-0722-5 |s2cid=122155922 |author-link1=Joshua N. Goldberg |author-link2=Rainer K. Sachs}}; originally published in Acta Phys. Pol. '''22''', 13–23 (1962).</ref>
* 1962 – Ehlers introduces [[Ehlers transformation]]s, a new [[solution generating method]],
* 1962 – [[Richard Arnowitt]], [[Stanley Deser]], and Charles W. Misner introduce the [[ADM formalism|ADM reformulation]] and [[global hyperbolicity]],
* 1962 – Istvan Ozsvath and [[Englbert Schücking]] rediscover the [[Ozváth-Schücking metric|circularly polarized monochromomatic gravitational wave]].
* 1962 – [[Hans Adolph Buchdahl]] discovers [[Buchdahl's theorem]].
* 1962 – Hermann Bondi introduces [[Bondi mass]].
* 1962 – Hermann Bondi, M. G. van der Burg, A. W. Metzner, and [[Rainer K. Sachs]] introduce the [[Bondi–Metzner–Sachs group|asymptotic symmetry group]] of [[Asymptotically flat spacetime|asymptotically flat]], Lorentzian spacetimes at null (''i.e.'', light-like) infinity.
* 1962 – [[Riccardo Giacconi]] and his team discover [[Astrophysical X-ray source|astronomical X-ray sources]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Giacconi|first1=R.|last2=Gursky|first2=H.|last3=Waters|first3=J. R.|last4=Clark|first4=G.|last5=RossI|first5=B.|date=December 1964|title=Two Sources of Cosmic X-rays in Scorpius and Sagittarius|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/204981a0|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=204|issue=4962|pages=981–982|doi=10.1038/204981a0|bibcode=1964Natur.204..981G|s2cid=4167564|issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=X-ray Astronomy |url=https://imagine.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/science/know_l2/history_xray.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090813003332/https://imagine.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/science/know_l2/history_xray.html |archive-date=August 13, 2009 |access-date=January 23, 2026 |website=Goddard Space Flight Center |publisher=National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)|date=August 22, 2009}}</ref>
* 1963 – [[Roy Kerr]] discovers the [[Kerr metric|Kerr solution]],<ref name="kerr_1963">{{cite journal |last=Kerr |first=Roy P. |author-link=Roy Kerr |date=1963 |title=Gravitational Field of a Spinning Mass as an Example of Algebraically Special Metrics |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=237–238 |bibcode=1963PhRvL..11..237K |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237}}</ref> subsequently shown by [[Boyer–Lindquist coordinates|Robert Boyer and Richard Lindquist]]<ref name="boyer_lindquist_1967">{{cite journal |last1=Boyer|first1=Robert H.|last2=Lindquist|first2=Richard W.|year=1967|title=Maximal Analytic Extension of the Kerr Metric|journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics|volume=8|issue=2|pages=265–281|doi=10.1063/1.1705193|bibcode=1967JMP.....8..265B}}</ref> and, independently, Brandon Carter and Roger Penrose to be describing a spinning black hole.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=542}}
* 1963 – Newman, T. Unti and L.A. Tamburino introduce the [[NUT vacuum solution]],
* 1963 – [[Roger Penrose]] introduces [[Penrose diagram]]s and [[Penrose limit]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Penrose |first=Roger |date=1963 |title=Asymptotic Properties of Fields and Space-Times |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=10 |issue=66 |pages=66–68 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.10.66|bibcode=1963PhRvL..10...66P |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1963 – [[Maarten Schmidt]], [[Jesse L. Greenstein|Jesse Greenstein]], and [[Allan Sandage]] discover the first quasi-stellar radio source (QSRS), [[3C 273|3C273]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=February 5, 1963: Maarten Schmidt Discovers First Known Quasar |url=https://www.aps.org/apsnews/2021/02/maarten-schmidt-discovers-first-quasar |access-date=February 25, 2026 |work=APS News |department=This Month in Physics History |publisher=American Physical Society (APS)}}</ref><ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=541}} later renamed "[[quasar]]" by [[Hong-Yee Chiu]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chiu |first1=Hong-Yee |date=May 1964 |title=Gravitational collapse |journal=Physics Today |volume=17 |issue=5 |pages=21–34 |bibcode=1964PhT....17e..21C |doi=10.1063/1.3051610 |quote=So far, the clumsily long name 'quasi-stellar radio sources' is used to describe these objects. Because the nature of these objects is entirely unknown, it is hard to prepare a short, appropriate nomenclature for them so that their essential properties are obvious from their name. For convenience, the abbreviated form 'quasar' will be used throughout this paper.|doi-access=free }}</ref> and shown to be moving away from Earth due to the expansion of the Universe.<ref name=":22" />
* 1963 – First [[Texas Symposium on Relativistic Astrophysics]] held in Dallas, December 16–18.<ref name=":04">{{Cite journal |last=Schücking |first=Engelbert |date=August 1989 |title=The First Texas Symposium on Relativistic Astrophysics |url=https://physicstoday.aip.org/features/the-first-texas-symposium-on-relativistic-astrophysics |journal=Physics Today |volume=42 |issue=8 |pages=46–52 |doi=10.1063/1.881214|bibcode=1989PhT....42h..46S |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":22" />
* 1964 – [[Steven Weinberg]] shows that a quantum field theory of interacting massless spin-2 particles is Lorentz invariant only if it satisfies the principle of equivalence.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weinberg |first=Steven |date=1964 |title=Derivation of gauge invariance and the equivalence principle from Lorentz invariance of the S-matrix |journal=Physics Letters |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=357–359 |bibcode=1964PhL.....9..357W |doi=10.1016/0031-9163(64)90396-8}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weinberg |first=Steven |date=1964 |title=Photons and gravitons in S-matrix theory: derivation of charge conservation and equality of gravitational and inertial mass |journal=Physical Review |volume=135 |issue=4B |pages=B1049–B1056 |bibcode=1964PhRv..135.1049W |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.135.B1049}}</ref><ref name=":20" />
* 1964 – [[Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar]] determines a stability criterion.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chandrasekhar |first=Subrahmanyan |date=1964 |title=Dynamical instability of gaseous masses approaching the Schwarzschild limit in general relativity |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.12.114 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=12 |issue=4 |pages=114–116 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.12.114|bibcode=1964PhRvL..12..114C |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1964 – [[Sjur Refsdal]] suggests that the Hubble constant could be determined using gravitational lensing.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Refsdal |first=Sjur |date=1964 |title=On the Possibility of Determining Hubble's Parameter and the Masses of Galaxies from the Gravitational Lens Effect |url=https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/128/4/307/2601707 |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |volume=128 |issue=4 |pages=307–310 |doi=10.1093/mnras/128.4.307|doi-access=free }}</ref>

* 1965 – Roger Penrose proves the first [[Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems|singularity theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Penrose |first=Roger |date=1965 |title=Gravitational Collapse and Space-Time Singularities |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=14 |issue=57 |pages=57–59 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57|bibcode=1965PhRvL..14...57P |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":22" />
* 1965 – [[Ezra T. Newman|Ezra Newman]] and others introduce [[Kerr–Newman metric|Kerr-Newman metric]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Newman |first1=Ezra |last2=Janis |first2=Allen |date=1965 |title=Note on the Kerr Spinning-Particle Metric |journal=[[Journal of Mathematical Physics]] |volume=6 |issue=6 |pages=915–917 |bibcode=1965JMP.....6..915N |doi=10.1063/1.1704350}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Newman |first1=Ezra |last2=Couch |first2=E. |last3=Chinnapared |first3=K. |last4=Exton |first4=A. |last5=Prakash |first5=A. |last6=Torrence |first6=R. |date=1965 |title=Metric of a Rotating, Charged Mass |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |volume=6 |issue=6 |pages=918–919 |bibcode=1965JMP.....6..918N |doi=10.1063/1.1704351}}</ref>
* 1965 – [[Arno Penzias]] and [[Robert Woodrow Wilson|Robert Wilson]] accidentally discover the [[cosmic microwave background radiation]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Penzias |first1=A.A. |last2=Wilson |first2=R.W. |date=1965 |title=A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s |journal=[[Astrophysical Journal]] |volume=142 |pages=419–421 |bibcode=1965ApJ...142..419P |doi=10.1086/148307|doi-access=free }}</ref> This supports the Big Bang model<ref name=":25" /><ref name=":52" />{{Reference page|page=106}} and rules out the [[steady-state model]] of [[Fred Hoyle]] and [[Jayant Narlikar]].<ref name=":22" />
* 1967 – John Archibald Wheeler popularizes "black hole" at a conference.<ref name=":6" />{{Reference page|pages=31-2}}<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bartusiak |first=Marcia |title=Black Hole: How an Idea Abandoned by Newtonians, Hated by Einstein, and Gambled on by Hawking Became Loved |publisher=[[Yale University Press]] |year=2015 |isbn=978-0-300-21085-9 |location=New Haven, CT |chapter=Chapter 9: Why Don't You Call It A Black Hole? |author-link=Marcia Bartusiak}}</ref>

* 1967 – [[Robert H. Boyer]] and [[R. W. Lindquist]] introduce [[Boyer–Lindquist coordinates]] for the Kerr vacuum.
* 1967 – [[Bryce DeWitt]] publishes on canonical quantum gravity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Deutsch |first1=David |last2=Isham |first2=Christopher |last3=Vilkovisky |first3=Gregory |date=2005 |title=Bryce Seligman DeWitt |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/58/3/84/1017002/Bryce-Seligman-DeWitt |journal=Physics Today |volume=58 |issue=3 |page=84 |doi=10.1063/1.1897570|bibcode=2005PhT....58c..84D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

* 1967 – [[Mendel Sachs]] publishes factorization of Einstein's field equations.
* 1967 – [[Hans Stephani]] discovers the [[Stephani dust solution]].
* 1968 – [[F. J. Ernst]] discovers the [[Ernst equation]].
* 1968 – [[B. Kent Harrison]] discovers the [[Harrison transformation]], a solution-generating method.
* 1968 – [[Brandon Carter]] solves the geodesic equations for Kerr–Newmann electrovacuum with [[Carter constant|Carter's constant]].<ref name="carter_1968">{{cite journal |last=Carter |first=Brandon |year=1968 |title=Global structure of the Kerr family of gravitational fields |journal=Physical Review |volume=174 |issue=5 |pages=1559&ndash;1571 |bibcode=1968PhRv..174.1559C |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.174.1559 |author-link=Brandon Carter}}</ref>

* 1968 – [[Kenneth Nordtvedt]] studies [[Nordtvedt effect|a possible violation of the weak equivalence principle]] for self-gravitating bodies and proposes a new test of the weak equivalence principle based on observing the relative motion of the Earth and Moon in the Sun's gravitational field.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nordvedt |first=Kennet |date=1968 |title=Equivalence Principle for Massive Bodies. * 1968-70 – Roger Penrose, [[Stephen Hawking]], and [[George F. R. ===1970s===
* 1970 – [[Vladimir Belinski|Vladimir Alekseevich Belinski]], [[Isaak Markovich Khalatnikov]], and [[Evgeny Lifshitz]] introduce the [[BKL conjecture]]. [[File:Apollo_15_feather_and_hammer_drop.ogv|right|thumb|Using a hammer and a feather on the Moon during [[Apollo 15]], David Scott validates Galileo's claim that objects in a vacuum will fall at the same rate.]]
* 1970 – Stephen Hawking and Roger Penrose prove trapped surfaces must arise in black holes.
* 1970 – [[Richard H. Price|Richard Price]] discovers Price's theorem.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=543}}
* 1971 – [[David Scott]] demonstrates that a hammer and a feather fall at the same rate on the Moon.<ref name=":11" />
* 1971 – Alfred Goldhaber and Michael Nieto give stringent limits on the photon mass.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Goldhaber |first1=Alfred |last2=Nieto |first2=Michael |date=1971 |title=Terrestrial and Extraterrestrial Limits on The Photon Mass |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.43.277 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |publisher=American Physical Society |volume=43 |issue=3 |pages=277–296 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.43.277|bibcode=1971RvMP...43..277G |url-access=subscription }}</ref> The strictest one is <math>m_{\gamma} \leq 4 \times 10^{-51} \text{kg}</math>.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Jackson |first=John David |title=Classical Electrodynamics |title-link=Classical Electrodynamics (book) |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |year=1999 |isbn=0-471-30932-X |edition=3rd |location=New York |pages= |chapter= |author-link=John David Jackson (physicist)}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=5-9}}
* 1971 – Stephen Hawking proves that the area of a black hole can never decrease.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hawking |first=Stephen |date=May 24, 1971 |title=Gravitational Radiation from Colliding Black Holes |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.26.1344 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=26 |issue=1344 |pages=1344–1346 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.26.1344 |bibcode=1971PhRvL..26.1344H }}</ref><ref name=":22" />
* 1971 – [[Peter C. Aichelburg]] and [[Roman U. Sexl]] introduce the [[Aichelburg–Sexl ultraboost]].
* 1971 – Introduction of the [[Khan–Penrose vacuum]], a simple explicit colliding plane wave spacetime.
* 1971 – [[Robert H. Gowdy]] introduces the [[Gowdy vacuum solutions]] (cosmological models containing circulating gravitational waves).[[File:Chandra image of Cygnus X-1.jpg|thumb|Image of Cygnus X-1 by the [[Chandra X-ray Observatory]] (2009)]]
* 1971 – [[Cygnus X-1]], the first solid black hole candidate, discovered by [[Uhuru (satellite)|Uhuru satellite]].<ref name=":22" />
* 1971 – [[William H. Press]] discovers by [[numerical relativity|numerical simulation]] that black holes can pulsate.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=543}}
* 1971 – [[Robert Geroch]] introduces [[Geroch group]]
* 1972 – [[Kip Thorne]] states the [[hoop conjecture]].<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=543}}
* 1972 – [[Jacob Bekenstein]] proposes that black holes have a non-decreasing [[entropy]] which can be identified with the area.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bekenstein |first1=A. |year=1972 |title=Black holes and the second law |journal=Lettere al Nuovo Cimento |volume=4 |issue=15 |pages=99–104 |doi=10.1007/BF02757029 |s2cid=120254309}}</ref><ref name=":22" />
* 1972 – Sachs introduces [[optical scalars]] and proves [[peeling theorem]].
* 1972 – [[Rainer Weiss]] proposes concept of gravitational-wave detector using [[laser interferometry]] in an unpublished manuscript.<ref>Cho, Adrian (October 3, 2017). "[https://www.science.org/content/article/ripples-space-us-trio-wins-physics-nobel-discovery-gravitational-waves Ripples in space: U.S. trio wins physics Nobel for discovery of gravitational waves]," ''Science''. Retrieved May 20, 2019.</ref>
* 1972 – [[Joseph C. Hafele|Joseph Hafele]] and [[Richard E. Keating|Richard Keating]] perform the [[Hafele–Keating experiment]].<ref name="paper1">{{Cite journal |last1=Hafele |first1=J. C. |last2=Keating |first2=R. E. |date=July 14, 1972 |title=Around-the-World Atomic Clocks: Predicted Relativistic Time Gains |url=http://www.personal.psu.edu/rq9/HOW/Atomic_Clocks_Predictions.pdf |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=177 |issue=4044 |pages=166–168 |bibcode=1972Sci...177..166H |doi=10.1126/science.177.4044.166 |pmid=17779917 |s2cid=10067969 |ref={{harvid|Hafele|Keating|1972a}}}}</ref><ref name="paper2">{{Cite journal |last1=Hafele |first1=J. C. |last2=Keating |first2=R. E. |date=July 14, 1972 |title=Around-the-World Atomic Clocks: Observed Relativistic Time Gains |url=http://www.personal.psu.edu/rq9/HOW/Atomic_Clocks_Experiment.pdf |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=177 |issue=4044 |pages=168–170 |bibcode=1972Sci...177..168H |doi=10.1126/science.177.4044.168 |pmid=17779918 |s2cid=37376002 |ref={{harvid|Hafele|Keating|1972b}}}}</ref><ref name="New Scientist 1972">{{cite journal |last=Wick |first=Gerald |date=February 3, 1972 |title=The clock paradox resolved |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BAIlXPgcsHwC&pg=PA261 |journal=New Scientist |pages=261&ndash;263}}</ref>
* 1972 – [[Saul Teukolsky]] derives the [[Teukolsky Equation|Teukolsky equation]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Teukolsky |first=Saul |date=1972 |title=Rotating black holes: Separable wave equations for gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations |url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/88198/1/PhysRevLett.29.1114.pdf |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=29 |issue=16 |pages=1114–1118|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.29.1114 |bibcode=1972PhRvL..29.1114T |s2cid=122083437 }}</ref>
* 1972 – [[Yakov B. Zel'dovich]] and [[Alexei Starobinsky]] speculate that black holes could radiate using [[quantum field theory in curved spacetime]].<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=543}}
* 1972 – [[James M. Bardeen|James Bardeen]] calculates the [[shadow]] of a black hole.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bardeen |first=James M. |date=1973 |title=Timelike and null geodesics in the Kerr metric |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sUr-EVqZLckC&dq=james+bardeen&pg=PA215 |journal=Proceedings, École d'Été de Physique Théorique: Les Astres Occlus: Les Houches, France, August, 1972 |pages=215–240|bibcode=1973blho.conf..215B |isbn=978-0-677-15610-1 }}</ref> This is later verified by the Event Horizon Telescope.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Overbye |first=Dennis |date=July 3, 2022 |title=James Bardeen, an Expert on Unraveling Einstein's Equations, Dies at 83 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/03/science/space/james-bardeen-an-expert-on-unraveling-einsteins-equations-dies-at-83.html |access-date=May 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220703204112/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/03/science/space/james-bardeen-an-expert-on-unraveling-einsteins-equations-dies-at-83.html |archive-date=July 3, 2022}}</ref>
* 1973 – [[Ray Klebesadel]], Ian Strong, and Roy Olson report their detection of the first cosmic [[Gamma-ray burst|gamma-ray bursts]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Klebesadel |first1=Ray W. |last2=Strong |first2=Ian B. |last3=Olson |first3=Roy A. |date=June 1973 |title=Observations of Gamma-Ray Bursts of Cosmic Origin |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1973ApJ...182L..85K/abstract |journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=182 |pages=L85 |doi=10.1086/181225 |bibcode=1973ApJ...182L..85K }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bonnell |first1=J. W. |date=1996 |title=A brief history of the discovery of cosmic gamma-ray bursts |journal=AIP Conference Proceedings |volume=384 |issue=977 |pages=977–980 |doi=10.1063/1.51630 |bibcode=1996AIPC..384..977B }}</ref>
* 1973 – Brandon Carter, Stephen Hawking, and James Bardeen propose the four [[laws of black hole mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bardeen |first1=John M. |last2=Carter |first2=Brandon |last3=Hawking |first3=Stephen |date=June 1973 |title=The four laws of black hole mechanics |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-31/issue-2/The-four-laws-of-black-hole-mechanics/cmp/1103858973.pdf |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=31 |issue=2 |pages=161–170 |bibcode=1973CMaPh..31..161B |doi=10.1007/BF01645742 |s2cid=54690354}}</ref><ref name=":22" />
* 1973 – [[Charles W. Misner]], Kip Thorne and John Archibald Wheeler publish the treatise ''[[Gravitation (book)|Gravitation]]'', a textbook that remains in use in the twenty-first century.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaiser |first=David |author-link=David Kaiser (physicist) |date=2012 |title=A Tale of Two Textooks |url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/664983 |journal=Isis |publisher=University of Chicago Press |volume=103 |issue=1|pages=126–138 |doi=10.1086/664983 |pmid=22655343 |hdl=1721.1/82907 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Dahn |first=Ryan |date=March 10, 2023 |title=Gravitation's attraction, 50 years later |work=Physics Today |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/online/41279/Gravitation-s-attraction-50-years-later |access-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref>
* 1973 – [[Stephen W. Hawking]] and [[George Francis Rayner Ellis|George Ellis]] publish the monograph ''[[The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time]]''.<ref name=":222">{{Cite book |last1=Hawking|first1=Stephen|title=My Brief History|publisher=Bantam Books|year=2013|isbn=978-0-345-53528-3|location=New York}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=64}}
* 1973 – Robert Geroch introduces the [[GHP formalism]].
* 1973 – Homer Ellis obtains the [[Ellis drainhole]],<ref name="ellis12">{{cite journal |author=H. G. Ellis |year=1973 |title=Ether flow through a drainhole: A particle model in general relativity |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=104–118 |bibcode=1973JMP....14..104E |doi=10.1063/1.1666161}}</ref> the first traversable wormhole.
* 1974 – [[Russell Alan Hulse]] and [[Joseph Hooton Taylor Jr.]] discover the [[PSR 1913+16|Hulse–Taylor binary pulsar]], which they used as an indirect test of orbital decay due to gravitational radiation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hulse |first1=Russell A. |last2=Taylor Jr. |first2=Joseph H. |date=1975 |title=Discovery of a Pulsar in a Binary System |journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=195 |pages=L51–L53 |doi=10.1086/181708 |bibcode=1975ApJ...195L..51H }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Weisberg |first1=Joel M. |last2=Taylor |first2=Joseph H. |last3=Fowler |first3=Lee A. |date=October 1981 |title=Gravitational Waves from an Orbiting Pulsar |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/gravitational-waves-from-an-orbitin/ |journal=Scientific American |volume=245 |issue=4 |pages=74–82 |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican1081-74 |bibcode=1981SciAm.245d..74W |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* [[File:BH-JPL-A&A1979.jpg|alt=Computer simulation of a black hole accretion disk published in 1979 by Jean-Pierre Luminet|thumb|Computer simulation of a black hole accretion disk published in 1979 by Jean-Pierre Luminet]]1974 – [[James W. York]] and Niall Ó Murchadha present the analysis of the initial value formulation and examine the stability of its solutions.
* 1974 – R. O. Hansen introduces [[Hansen–Geroch multipole moment]]s.
* 1974 – Stephen Hawking discovers [[Hawking radiation]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Matson |date=October 1, 2010 |title=Artificial event horizon emits laboratory analogue to theoretical black hole radiation |url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/hawking-radiation/ |journal=Scientific American|first=John}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hawking |first=Stephen |date=March 1, 1974 |title=Black Hole Explosions? |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/248030a0 |journal=Nature |volume=248 |issue=5443 |pages=30–31 |doi=10.1038/248030a0|bibcode=1974Natur.248...30H |s2cid=4290107 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1975 – Stephen Hawking shows that [[Bekenstein-Hawking entropy equation|the area of a black hole is proportional to its entropy]], as previously conjectured by Jacob Bekenstein.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hawking |first=Stephen |date=1975 |title=Particle Creation by Black Holes |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02345020 |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=43 |issue=3 |pages=199–220 |doi=10.1007/BF02345020|bibcode=1975CMaPh..43..199H |s2cid=55539246 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1975 – Roberto Colella, [[Albert Overhauser]], and Samuel Werner observe the quantum-mechanical phase shift of neutrons due to gravity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Collela |first1=Roberto |last2=Overhauser |first2=Albert |last3=Werner |first3=Samuel |date=1975 |title=Observation of Gravitationally Induced Quantum Interference |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1472 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=34 |issue=1472 |pages=1472–1474 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1472|bibcode=1975PhRvL..34.1472C |url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[Neutron interferometer|Neutron interferometry]] was later used to test the principle of equivalence.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Staudenmann |first1=J. -L. |last2=Collela |first2=Roberto |last3=Werner |first3=Samuel |last4=Overhauser |first4=Albert |date=1980 |title=Gravity and Inertia in Quantum Mechanics |url=https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.21.1419 |journal=Physical Review A |volume=21 |issue=1419 |pages=1419–1438 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.21.1419|bibcode=1980PhRvA..21.1419S |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abele |first1=Hartmut |last2=Leeb |first2=Helmut |date=2012 |title=Gravitation and quantum interference experiments with neutrons |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1367-2630/14/5/055010 |journal=New Journal of Physics |volume=14 |issue=5 |article-number=055010 |doi=10.1088/1367-2630/14/5/055010 |issn=1367-2630|arxiv=1207.2953 |bibcode=2012NJPh...14e5010A |s2cid=53653704 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Townsend |first=John S. |title=A Modern Approach to Quantum Mechanics |publisher=University Science Books |year=2012 |isbn=978-1-891389-78-8 |edition=2nd |pages=297–99 |chapter=Section 8.7: Quantum Interference due to Gravity}}</ref>
* 1975 – Chandrasekhar and [[Steven Detweiler]] compute the effects of perturbations on a Schwarzschild black hole.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chandrasekhar |first1=S. |last2=Detweiler |first2=S. |date=1975 |title=The quasi-normal modes of the Schwarzchild black hole |journal=Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A |volume=344 |issue=1639 |pages=441–452 |bibcode=1975RSPSA.344..441C |doi=10.1098/rspa.1975.0112}}</ref>
* 1977 – [[Roger Blandford]] and Roman Znajek propose the [[Blandford–Znajek process]] to explain how quasars are powered.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blandford|first1=R. D.|last2=Znajek|first2=R. L.|date=1977-07-01|title=Electromagnetic extraction of energy from Kerr black holes|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume=179|issue=3|pages=433–456|doi=10.1093/mnras/179.3.433|doi-access=free|issn=0035-8711|arxiv=astro-ph/0506302|bibcode=1977MNRAS.179..433B}}</ref>
* 1978 – Belinskiǐ and Zakharov show how to solve [[Einstein's field equations]] using the [[inverse scattering transform]]; the first [[gravitational soliton]]s,
* 1979 – [[Dennis Walsh]], [[Robert Carswell (scientist)|Robert Carswell]], and [[Ray Weymann]] discover the gravitationally lensed [[quasar]] [[Q0957+561]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=D.Walsh |author2=R.F.Carswell |author3=R.J.Weymann |date=31 May 1979 |title=0957 + 561 A, B: twin quasistellar objects or gravitational lens? |url=http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v279/n5712/pdf/279381a0.pdf |journal=Nature |volume=279 |issue=5712 |pages=381–384 |doi=10.1038/279381a0 |pmid=16068158 |bibcode=1979Natur.279..381W |s2cid=2142707}}</ref>
* 1979 – [[Jean-Pierre Luminet]] creates an image of a black hole with an [[accretion disk]] using computer simulation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Luminet |first=Jean-Pierre |date=1979 |title=Image of a spherical black hole with thin accretion disk |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1979A%26A....75..228L |journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics |volume=75 |issue=1–2 |pages=228–235|bibcode=1979A&A....75..228L }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=April 10, 2019 |title=First ever image of a black hole: a CNRS researcher had simulated it as early as 1979 |work=Espace presse |publisher=[[CNRS]] |url=https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/node/3764 |access-date=May 24, 2023}}</ref>
* 1979 – Steven Detweiler proposes using [[pulsar timing array]]s to detect gravitational waves.<ref name="DetweilerPulsarTiming">{{cite journal |last1=Detweiler |first1=Steven L. |date=1979 |title=Pulsar timing measurements and the search for gravitational waves |journal=Astrophys. * 1979-81 – [[Richard Schoen]] and [[Shing-Tung Yau]] prove the [[positive energy theorem|positive mass theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schoen |first1=Robert |last2=Yau |first2=Shing-Tung |year=1979 |title=On the proof of the positive mass conjecture in general relativity |url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1103904790 |journal=[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]] |volume=65 |issue=1 |page=45 |bibcode=1979CMaPh..65...45S |doi=10.1007/BF01940959 |s2cid=54217085}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schoen |first1=Robert |last2=Yau |first2=Shing-Tung |year=1981 |title=Proof of the positive mass theorem. === 1980s ===
[[File:COBE cmb fluctuations.png|alt=Variations in the temperature of the cosmic microwave background measured by the COBE satellite.|thumb|Variations in the temperature of the cosmic microwave background measured by the COBE satellite. The plane of the Milky Way Galaxy is horizontal across the middle of each picture.]]
* 1980 – [[Vera Rubin]] and colleagues study the rotational properties of [[UGC 2885]], demonstrating the prevalence of dark matter.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rubin |first1=Vera |last2=Ford |first2=W. K. |display-authors=1 |date=June 1980 |title=Rotational properties of 21 SC galaxies with a large range of luminosities and radii, from NGC 4605 (R=4kpc) to UGC 2885 (R=122kpc) |journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=238 |pages=471–487 |doi=10.1086/158003|bibcode=1980ApJ...238..471R |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Nemiroff |first1=Robert |last2=Bonnell |first2=Jerry |date=April 5, 2023 |title=Rubin's Galaxy |url=https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/ap230405.html |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=Astronomy Picture of the Day |publisher=[[NASA]]}}</ref>
* 1980 – [[Gravity Probe A]] verifies gravitational redshift to approximately 0.007% using a space-born [[hydrogen maser]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vessot |first1=R. F. C. |last2=Levine |first2=M. W. |display-authors=1 |date=1980 |title=Test of Relativistic Gravitation with a Space-Borne Hydrogen Maser |url=http://personal.psu.edu/rq9/HOW/Gravity_test_with_Space_Maser.pdf |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=45 |issue=26 |pages=2081–2084 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.2081|bibcode=1980PhRvL..45.2081V }}</ref>
* 1980 – James Bardeen explains structure in the Universe using [[cosmological perturbation theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bardeen |first=James M. |date=1980 |title=Gauge-invariant cosmological perturbations |url=http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~wzhao7/c_index_files/main.files/bardeen.pdf |journal=Physical Review D |volume=22 |issue=8 |pages=1882–1905 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.22.1882|bibcode=1980PhRvD..22.1882B }}</ref>
* 1981 – [[Alan Guth]] proposes [[Inflation (cosmology)|cosmic inflation]] in order to solve the [[Flatness problem|flatness]] and [[horizon problem]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Guth |first=Alan |author-link=Alan Guth |date=15 January 1981 |title=Inflationary universe: A possible solution to the horizon and flatness problems |journal=[[Physical Review D]] |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=347–356 |bibcode=1981PhRvD..23..347G |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.23.347 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* 1982 – [[Joseph Hooton Taylor, Jr.|Joseph Taylor]] and [[Joel Weisberg]] show that the rate of energy loss from the binary [[pulsar]] [[PSR B1913+16]] agrees with that predicted by the general relativistic [[quadrupole formula]] to within 5%.<ref name="tw82">{{cite journal |last1=Taylor |first1=J. H. |last2=Weisberg |first2=J. M. |date=1982 |title=A new test of general relativity – Gravitational radiation and the binary pulsar PSR 1913+16 |journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=253 |pages=908–920 |bibcode=1982ApJ...253..908T |doi=10.1086/159690}}</ref>
* 1983 – James Hartle and Stephen Hawking propose the [[Hartle–Hawking state|no-boundary wave function]] for the Universe.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hartle|first1=James B.|last2=Hawking|first2=Stephen W.|date=December 15, 1983|title=Wave Function of the Universe|url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.28.2960|journal=[[Physical Review D]]|volume=28|issue=2960|pages=2960–2975 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.28.2960 |bibcode=1983PhRvD..28.2960H }}</ref><ref name=":52">{{Cite book |last=Ferguson|first=Kitty|author-link=Kitty Ferguson|title=Stephen Hawking: An Unfettered Mind|publisher=Palgrave MacMillan|year=2012|isbn=978-0-230-34060-2}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=129}}
* 1983-84 – [[RELIKT-1]] observes the cosmic microwave background.
* 1984 – The U.S. [[National Science Foundation]] agrees to fund the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory ([[LIGO]]) project.<ref name=":92" />{{Reference page|page=545}}
* 1986 – Helmut Friedrich proves that the [[de Sitter space]]time is stable.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Friedrich |first=Helmut |date=1986 |title=On the existence of <math>n</math>-geodesically complete or future complete solutions of Einstein's field equations with smooth asymptotic structure |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-107/issue-4/On-the-existence-of-n-geodesically-complete-or-future-complete/cmp/1104116232.full |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=107 |issue=4 |pages=587–609|doi=10.1007/BF01205488 |bibcode=1986CMaPh.107..587F |s2cid=121761845 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Nadis |first=Steve |date=May 11, 2020 |title=New Math Proves That a Special Kind of Space-Time Is Unstable |work=Quanta Magazine |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/new-math-proves-that-a-special-kind-of-space-time-is-unstable-20200511/# |access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref>
* 1986 – [[Bernard F. Schutz|Bernard Schutz]] shows that cosmic distances can be determined using sources of gravitational waves without references to the [[cosmic distance ladder]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schultz |first=Bernard |date=1986 |title=Determining the Hubble constant from gravitational wave observations |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/323310a0 |journal=Nature |volume=323 |issue=6086 |pages=310–311 |doi=10.1038/323310a0|bibcode=1986Natur.323..310S |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-73C1-2 |s2cid=4327285 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Standard-siren astronomy is born.
* 1988 – [[Mike Morris (physicist)|Mike Morris]], Kip Thorne, and [[Yurtsever Ulvi]] obtain the [[Morris-Thorne wormhole]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Morris |first1=Mike |last2=Thorne |first2=Kip |last3=Yurtsever |first3=Ulvi |date=1986 |title=Wormholes, Time Machines, and the Weak Energy Condition |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.1446 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=61 |issue=1446 |pages=1446–1449 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.1446|pmid=10038800 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Morris and Thorne argue for its pedagogical value.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Morris, Michael S. |author2=Thorne, Kip S. |name-list-style=amp |year=1988 |title=Wormholes in spacetime and their use for interstellar travel: A tool for teaching general relativity |journal=[[American Journal of Physics]] |volume=56 |issue=5 |pages=395–412 |bibcode=1988AmJPh..56..395M |doi=10.1119/1.15620|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1989 – [[Steven Weinberg]] discusses the [[cosmological constant problem]], the discrepancy between the measured value and those predicted by modern theories of elementary particles.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weinberg |first=Steven |date=1989 |title=The Cosmological Constant Problem |url=https://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=61 |issue=1 |pages=1–23 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1|bibcode=1989RvMP...61....1W |hdl=2152/61094 |s2cid=122259372 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
* 1989-93 – The [[Cosmic Background Explorer]] (COBE) identifies anisotropy in the cosmic microwave background.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Smoot |first=G. F. |display-authors=etal |date=1992 |title=Structure in the COBE differential microwave radiometer first-year maps |journal=[[Astrophysical Journal Letters]] |volume=396 |issue=1 |pages=L1–L5 |bibcode=1992ApJ...396L...1S |doi=10.1086/186504 |s2cid=120701913 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Bennett |first=C.L. |display-authors=etal |year=1996 |title=Four-Year COBE DMR Cosmic Microwave Background Observations: Maps and Basic Results |journal=[[Astrophysical Journal Letters]] |volume=464 |pages=L1–L4 |arxiv=astro-ph/9601067 |bibcode=1996ApJ...464L...1B |doi=10.1086/310075 |s2cid=18144842}}</ref>

=== 1990s ===
[[File:GR2bodyparameterspace.png|thumb|280x280px|Parameter space of various approximation techniques in general relativity]]
* 1992 – Stephen Hawking states his [[chronology protection conjecture]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hawking |first=Stephen |date=1992 |title=Chronology Protection Conjecture |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.46.603 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=46 |issue=603 |pages=603–611 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.46.603|pmid=10014972 |bibcode=1992PhRvD..46..603H |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1993 – [[Demetrios Christodoulou]] and [[Sergiu Klainerman]] prove the non-linear stability of the [[Minkowski space]]time.<ref>{{cite book |author1=Christodoulou, Demetrios |title=The global nonlinear stability of the Minkowski space |author2=Klainerman, Sergiu |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |year=1993 |isbn=0-691-08777-6 |location=Princeton}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
* 1995 – [[John Donoghue (physicist)|John F. Donoghue]] shows that general relativity is a quantum [[effective field theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Donoghue |first=John F. |author1-link=John Francis Donoghue (physicist) |date=1994 |title=General relativity as an effective field theory: The leading quantum corrections |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.50.3874 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=50 |issue=3874 |pages=3874–3888 |arxiv=gr-qc/9405057 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.50.3874|pmid=10018030 |bibcode=1994PhRvD..50.3874D |s2cid=14352660 }}</ref> This framework could be used to analyze binary systems observed by gravitational-wave observatories.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Goldberger |first1=Walter |last2=Rothstein |first2=Ira |year=2004 |title=An Effective Field Theory of Gravity for Extended Objects |journal=Physical Review D |volume=73 |issue=10 |article-number=104029 |arxiv=hep-th/0409156 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.73.104029 |s2cid=54188791}}</ref>
* 1995 – [[Hubble Deep Field]] image taken.<ref name="Hubble_image">{{cite web |date=1995 |title=Hubble's Deepest View of the Universe Unveils Bewildering Galaxies across Billions of Years |url=http://hubblesite.org/newscenter/archive/releases/1996/01/image/a/ |access-date=January 12, 2009 |publisher=[[NASA]]}}</ref> It is a landmark in the study of cosmology.
* 1998 – The first complete [[Einstein ring]], [[B1938+666]], discovered using the [[Hubble Space Telescope]] and [[MERLIN]].<ref name="Bullseye">{{cite web |date=27 March 1998 |title=A Bull's Eye for MERLIN and the Hubble |url=https://www.merlin.ac.uk/press/PR9801/press.html |publisher=University of Manchester}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Browne |first=Malcolm W. |date=1998-03-31 |title='Einstein Ring' Caused by Space Warping Is Found |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9906EFDF103BF932A05750C0A96E958260 |access-date=2010-05-01}}</ref>
* 1998-99 – Scientists discover that the expansion of the Universe is [[Accelerating expansion of the universe|accelerating]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Reiss |first1=Adam G. |last2=Filippenko |first2=Alexei V. |last3=Challis |first3=Peter |last4=Clocchiatti |first4=Alejandro |last5=Diercks |first5=Alan |last6=Garnavich |first6=Peter M. |last7=Gilliland |first7=Ron L. |last8=Hogan |first8=Craig J. |last9=Jha |first9=Saurabh |last10=Kirshner |first10=Robert P. |last11=Leibundgut |first11=B. |last12=Phillips |first12=M. * 1999 – [[Alessandra Buonanno]] and [[Thibault Damour]] introduce the [[effective one-body formalism]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Buonanno |first1=A. |last2=Damour |first2=T. |date=1999-03-08 |title=Effective one-body approach to general relativistic two-body dynamics |journal=Physical Review D |publisher=American Physical Society (APS) |volume=59 |issue=8 |article-number=084006 |arxiv=gr-qc/9811091 |bibcode=1999PhRvD..59h4006B |doi=10.1103/physrevd.59.084006 |issn=0556-2821 |s2cid=14951569}}</ref> This is later used to analyze data collected by gravitational-wave observatories.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Abbott |first1=B. == 2000s ==
* 2003 – Arvind Borde, [[Alan Guth]], and [[Alexander Vilenkin]] prove the [[Borde–Guth–Vilenkin theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Borde |first1=Arvind |last2=Guth |first2=Alan H. |last3=Vilenkin |first3=Alexander |date=15 April 2003 |title=Inflationary space-times are incomplete in past directions |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=90 |issue=15 |article-number=151301 |arxiv=gr-qc/0110012 |bibcode=2003PhRvL..90o1301B |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.151301 |pmid=12732026 |s2cid=46902994}}</ref><ref name="Cosmocurious">{{cite book |last1=Perlov |first1=Delia |title=Cosmology for the Curious |last2=Vilenkin |first2=Alexander |date=7 August 2017 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-57040-2 |location=Cham, Switzerland |pages=330–31}}</ref>
* 2002 – First data collection of the [[LIGO|Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory]] (LIGO).
* 2002 – James Williams, Slava Turyshev, and Dale Boggs conduct stringent lunar test of violations of the principle of equivalence.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Williams |first1=James G. |last2=Turyshev |first2=Slava G. |last3=Boggs |first3=Dale H. |date=2004 |title=Progress in Lunar Laser Ranging Tests of Relativistic Gravity |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.261101 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=93 |issue=26 |article-number=261101 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.261101|pmid=15697965 |arxiv=gr-qc/0411113 |bibcode=2004PhRvL..93z1101W |s2cid=33664768 }}</ref>
* 2005 – [[Daniel Holz]] and Scott Hughes coin the term "[[standard sirens]]" in their study of gravitational waves.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Holz |first1=Daniel |last2=Hughes |first2=Scott |date=2005 |title=Using Gravitational-Wave Standard Sirens |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/431341 |journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=629 |issue=1 |pages=15–22 |doi=10.1086/431341|arxiv=astro-ph/0504616 |bibcode=2005ApJ...629...15H |hdl=1721.1/101190 |s2cid=12017349 }}</ref>
* 2005 – [[Frans Pretorius]] wrote the first computer simulation of merging black holes, a significant step in the development of [[numerical relativity]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Yau|first1=Shing-Tung|author-link1=Shing-Tung Yau|title=The Gravity of Math: How Geometry Rules the Universe|last2=Nadis|first2=Steve|publisher=Basic Books|year=2024|isbn=978-1-541-60429-2}}</ref>{{Reference page|pages=142-3}}
* 2009 – [[Gravity Probe B]] experiment verifies the geodetic effect and [[frame-dragging]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Everitt, C.W.F. |author2=Parkinson, B.W. |date=2009 |title=Gravity Probe B Science Results—NASA Final Report |url=https://einstein.stanford.edu/content/final_report/GPB_Final_NASA_Report-020509-web.pdf |access-date=2 May 2009}}</ref><ref name="PRL">{{cite journal |author=Everitt |display-authors=etal |date=2011 |title=Gravity Probe B: Final Results of a Space Experiment to Test General Relativity |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=106 |issue=22 |article-number=221101 |arxiv=1105.3456 |bibcode=2011PhRvL.106v1101E |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.221101 |pmid=21702590 |s2cid=11878715}}</ref>

===2010s===
[[File:PIA16874-CobeWmapPlanckComparison-20130321.jpg|thumb|280x280px|Improving cosmological measurements by three different satellites]]
* 2010 – A team at the U.S. [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|National Institute for Standards and Technology]] (NIST) verifies relativistic time dilation using optical [[atomic clock]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Chou, C. W. |author2=Hume, D. B. |author3=Rosenband, T. |author4=Wineland, D. J. |author-link4=David J. * 2011 – [[Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe]] (WMAP) finds no statistically significant deviations from the [[Lambda-CDM model|ΛCDM model]] of cosmology.<ref name="WMAP CMB">{{cite journal |last1=Bennett |first1=C. L. |display-authors=et al. |year=2011 |title=Seven-Year Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP) Observations: Are There Cosmic Microwave Background Anomalies? |journal=Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series |volume=192 |issue=2 |page=17 |arxiv=1001.4758 |bibcode=2011ApJS..192...17B |doi=10.1088/0067-0049/192/2/17 |s2cid=53521938}}</ref>
* 2012 – [[Hubble Ultra-Deep Field]] image released. It was created using data collected by the Hubble Space Telescope between 2003 and 2004.<ref name="xdf">{{cite web |date=September 25, 2012 |title=Hubble Goes to the eXtreme to Assemble Farthest-Ever View of the Universe |url=http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/hubble/science/xdf.html |access-date=September 26, 2012 |publisher=[[NASA]]}}</ref>
* 2013 – [[NuSTAR]] and [[XMM-Newton]] measure the spin of the [[supermassive black hole]] at the center of the galaxy [[NGC 1365]].<ref>{{cite news |date=27 February 2013 |title=NASA's NuSTAR Helps Solve Riddle of Black Hole Spin |publisher=[[NASA]]|url=http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/nustar/news/nustar20130227.html |access-date=3 March 2013}} {{PD-notice}}</ref>
* 2015 – Advanced LIGO reports the first direct detections of gravitational waves, [[GW150914]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=LIGO-VIRGO Collaboration |date=2016 |title=Tests of general relativity with GW150914 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.221101 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=116 |issue=22 |page=22110 |article-number=221101 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.221101|pmid=27314708 |arxiv=1602.03841 |bibcode=2016PhRvL.116v1101A |s2cid=217275338 }}</ref> and [[GW151226]],<ref name="PRL-20160615">{{Cite journal |last=Abbott |first=B. P. |date=15 June 2016 |title=GW151226: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a 22-Solar-Mass Binary Black Hole Coalescence |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=116 |issue=24 |article-number=241103 |arxiv=1606.04855 |bibcode=2016PhRvL.116x1103A |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.241103 |pmid=27367379 |collaboration=LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration |s2cid=118651851}}</ref> mergers of stellar-mass black holes. [[Gravitational-wave astronomy]] is born.<ref name="Naeye">{{cite news |last=Naeye |first=Robert |date=11 February 2016 |title=Gravitational Wave Detection Heralds New Era of Science |work=Sky and Telescope |url=http://www.skyandtelescope.com/astronomy-news/gravitational-wave-detection-heralds-new-era-of-science-0211201644/ |access-date=11 February 2016}}</ref> No deviations from general relativity were found.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pretorius |first=Frans |date=May 31, 2016 |title=Relativity Gets Thorough Vetting from LIGO |volume=9 |work=Physics |publisher=American Physical Society |issue=52 |url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v9/52 |access-date=May 12, 2023}}</ref><ref name="MIT">{{cite news |last=Chu |first=Jennifer |date=June 15, 2016 |title=For second time, LIGO detects gravitational waves |work=MIT News |url=https://news.mit.edu/2016/second-time-ligo-detects-gravitational-waves-0615 |access-date=June 16, 2016}}</ref>

* 2017 – [[Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer]] (NICER) arrives on the International Space Station.<ref name=":1" />
* 2017-18 – Georgios Moschidis proves the instability of the [[anti-de Sitter space]]time.<ref name=":0" />
* 2018 – Final paper by the [[Planck (spacecraft)|Planck satellite]] collaboration.<ref name="planck2018">{{cite journal |last=Akrami |first=Y. |display-authors=etal |year=2020 |title=''Planck'' 2018 results. I. * 2018 – Mihalis Dafermos and Jonathan Luk disprove the strong cosmic censorship hypothesis for the Cauchy horizon of an uncharged, rotating black hole.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Hartnett |first=Kevin |date=17 May 2018 |title=Mathematicians Disprove Conjecture Made to Save Black Holes |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematicians-disprove-conjecture-made-to-save-black-holes-20180517/ |magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]] |access-date=29 March 2020}}</ref>
* 2018 – [[European Southern Observatory]] (ESO) observes gravitational redshift of radiation emitted by matter orbiting [[Sagittarius A*]], the central supermassive black hole of the Milky Way,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=GRAVITY Collaboration |date=July 26, 2018 |title=Detection of the gravitational redshift in the orbit of the star S2 near the Galactic centre massive black hole⋆ |url=https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/abs/2018/07/aa33718-18/aa33718-18.html |journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics |volume=615 |issue=L15 |pages=L15 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201833718 |doi-access=free|arxiv=1807.09409 |bibcode=2018A&A...615L..15G }}</ref> and verifies the [[innermost stable circular orbit]] for that object.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=GRAVITY Collaboration |date=October 31, 2018 |title=Detection of orbital motions near the last stable circular orbit of the massive black hole SgrA*⋆ |url=https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/full_html/2018/10/aa34294-18/aa34294-18.html |journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics |volume=618 |issue=L10 |pages=L10 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201834294 |doi-access=free|arxiv=1810.12641 |bibcode=2018A&A...618L..10G }}</ref>
* 2018 –  Advanced LIGO-VIRGO collaboration constrains [[equations of state]] for a neutron star using GW170817.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Advanced LIGO-VIRGO Collaboration |date=2018 |title=GW170817: Measurements of Neutron Star Radii and Equation of State |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.161101 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=121 |issue=16 |article-number=161101 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.161101|pmid=30387654 |arxiv=1805.11581 |bibcode=2018PhRvL.121p1101A |s2cid=53235598 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sokol |first=Joshua |date=June 5, 2018 |title=Gravitational Waves Reveal the Hearts of Neutron Stars |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/gravitational-waves-reveal-the-hearts-of-neutron-stars1/ |journal=Scientific American|volume=1 |issue=3 |pages=None |doi=10.1038/scientificamericanspace0818-11 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 2018 – Luciano Rezzolla, Elias R. Most, and Lukas R. * 2018 – Kris Pardo, Maya Fishbach, Daniel Holz, and David Spergel limit the number of spacetime dimensions through which gravitational waves can propagate to 3 + 1, in line with general relativity and ruling out models that allow for "leakage" to higher dimensions of space.<ref name="arxiv.org 2">{{cite journal |last1=Pardo |first1=Kris |last2=Fishbach |first2=Maya |last3=Holz |first3=Daniel E. |last4=Spergel |first4=David N. |year=2018 |title=Limits on the number of spacetime dimensions from [[GW170817]] |journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics |volume=2018 |issue=7 |page=048 |arxiv=1801.08160 |bibcode=2018JCAP...07..048P |doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2018/07/048 |s2cid=119197181}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lerner |first=Louise |date=September 13, 2018 |title=Gravitational waves provide dose of reality about extra dimensions |work=UChicago News |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/gravitational-waves-provide-dose-reality-about-extra-dimensions |access-date=January 3, 2023}}</ref> Analyses of GW170817 have also ruled out many [[alternatives to general relativity]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=LIGO-VIRGO Collaboration|date=2018|title=Tests of General Relativity with GW170817|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.011102|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=123|issue=1|article-number=011102|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.011102|pmid=31386391|s2cid=119214541|arxiv=1811.00364}}</ref> such as scalar-tensor theory<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Lombriser L, Lima N |year=2017 |title=Challenges to self-acceleration in modified gravity from gravitational waves and large-scale structure |journal=Phys. Lett. B |volume=765 |pages=382–385 |arxiv=1602.07670 |bibcode=2017PhLB..765..382L |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2016.12.048 |s2cid=118486016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |first4=Miguel |vauthors=Bettoni D, Ezquiaga JM, Hinterbichler K, Zumalacárregui M |date=14 April 2017 |title=Speed of gravitational waves and the fate of Scalar-Tensor Gravity |journal=Physical Review&nbsp;D |volume=95 |issue=8 |article-number=084029 |arxiv=1608.01982 |bibcode=2017PhRvD..95h4029B |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.95.084029 |issn=2470-0010 |s2cid=119186001}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Sakstein J, Jain B|date=December 2017|title=Implications of the Neutron Star Merger GW170817 for Cosmological Scalar-Tensor Theories|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=119|issue=25|article-number=251303|arxiv=1710.05893|bibcode=2017PhRvL.119y1303S|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.251303|pmid=29303345|s2cid=39068360}}</ref> and [[bimetric gravity]],<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Baker T, Bellini E, Ferreira PG, Lagos M, Noller J, Sawicki I |date=December 2017 |title=Strong Constraints on Cosmological Gravity from GW170817 and GRB 170817A |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=119 |issue=25 |article-number=251301 |arxiv=1710.06394 |bibcode=2017PhRvL.119y1301B |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.251301 |pmid=29303333 |s2cid=36160359}}</ref> and proposals for dark energy.<ref name="Dark Energy after GW 170817">{{cite journal |vauthors=Creminelli P, Vernizzi F |date=December 2017 |title=Dark Energy after GW170817 and GRB170817A |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=119 |issue=25 |article-number=251302 |arxiv=1710.05877 |bibcode=2017PhRvL.119y1302C |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.251302 |pmid=29303308 |s2cid=206304918}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |vauthors=Boran S, Desai S, Kahya E, Woodard R |year=2018 |title=GW&nbsp;170817 falsifies dark matter emulators |journal=Phys. * 2019 – [[Event Horizon Telescope]] (EHT) releases an image of [[supermassive black hole]] [[Messier 87#Supermassive black hole M87*|M87*]], and measures its mass and shadow.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration |date=April 10, 2019 |title=First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. * 2019 – Advanced LIGO and VIRGO detect [[GW190814]], the collision of a 26-solar-mass black hole and a 2.6-solar-mass object, either an extremely heavy neutron star or a very light black hole.<ref name="LIGO-2020">{{cite news |author=Staff |date=2020 |title=GW190814 Factsheet: Lowest mass ratio to date: Strongest evidence of higher order modes |work=[[LIGO]] |url=https://dcc.ligo.org/public/0168/G2000846/002/GW190814%20Factsheet.pdf |access-date=26 June 2020}}</ref><ref name="AJL-20200623">{{cite journal |author=Abbott, R. |display-authors=et al. |date=23 June 2020 |title=GW190814: Gravitational Waves from the Coalescence of a 23 Solar Mass Black Hole with a 2.6 Solar Mass Compact Object |journal=[[The Astrophysical Journal Letters]] |volume=896 |pages=L44 |arxiv=2006.12611 |bibcode=2020ApJ...896L..44A |doi=10.3847/2041-8213/ab960f |doi-access=free |number=2}}</ref> This is the largest mass gap seen in a gravitational-wave source to-date.
